Step 3: Match item C (F = 20 N): F = 20 N reaches limiting friction, block is on verge of motion, f = 20 N. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (F = 30 N): F = 30 N > 20 N, block moves, so friction is kinetic: f_k = μ_k N = 0.3 × 50 = 15 N. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the friction definitions and relationships in List I with their descriptions in List II:
List I:
A. Angle of friction λ
B. Angle of repose θ_r
C. Rolling friction
D. Coefficient of kinetic friction μ_k
List II:
I. Much smaller than sliding friction, caused by surface deformation
II. Maximum incline angle at which a body rests without sliding down
III. Dimensionless ratio of kinetic friction to normal force, with μ_k < μ_s
IV. tan^-1(μ_s), angle between total contact reaction and normal reaction
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Angle of friction λ): By definition, tan λ = f_s,max / N = μ_s. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Angle of repose θ_r): At angle of repose, mg sin θ = μ_s mg cos θ -> tan θ_r = μ_s. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Rolling friction): Rolling friction arises due to deformation of contact surfaces and has a much lower coefficient. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Coefficient of kinetic friction μ_k): μ_k = f_k / N, generally less than static coefficient μ_s. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block of mass m = 2 kg is placed on an incline of angle θ = 30° with μ_s = 0.6 and μ_k = 0.5 (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each parameter in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Normal reaction force on the block
B. Maximum available limiting friction force
C. Actual static friction force acting on the block
D. Acceleration of the block down the incline
List II:
I. 10 N
II. 10√3 N
III. 0 m/s^2
IV. 6√3 N (~ 10.39 N)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Normal reaction force on the block): N = mg cos 30° = 2 × 10 × (√3/2) = 10√3 N. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum available limiting friction force): f_s,max = μ_s N = 0.6 × 10√3 = 6√3 N. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Actual static friction force acting on the block): Downhill gravity component = mg sin 30° = 2 × 10 × 0.5 = 10 N. Since 10 N < 6√3 N, block stays at rest and f = 10 N. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Acceleration of the block down the incline): Since downhill gravity is less than limiting friction, the block does not slide: a = 0 m/s^2. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A body of mass m = 10 kg is projected on a rough horizontal surface with initial speed u = 12 m/s (coefficient of kinetic friction μ_k = 0.3, g = 10 m/s^2). Match each kinematic parameter in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Deceleration of the body
B. Time taken to come to a complete stop
C. Stopping distance traveled
D. Total work done by friction on the body
List II:
I. 4 s
II. -720 J
III. 3 m/s^2
IV. 24 m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Deceleration of the body): a = μ_k g = 0.3 × 10 = 3 m/s^2. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Time taken to come to a complete stop): t = u / a = 12 / 3 = 4 s. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Stopping distance traveled): s = u^2 / (2a) = 144 / 6 = 24 m. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Total work done by friction on the body): W = ΔKE = 0 - (1/2)(10)(12)^2 = -720 J. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block of mass m = 10 kg rests on a rough floor with friction coefficient μ = 0.5 (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each force direction in List I with the minimum magnitude required to just move the block in List II:
List I:
A. Horizontal pulling force (θ = 0°)
B. Minimum pulling force at optimal angle θ = tan^-1(0.5)
C. Pulling force required at angle θ = 45° above the horizontal
D. Pushing force required at angle θ = 45° below the horizontal
List II:
I. 100√2/3 N (~ 47.1 N)
II. 50 N
III. 100√2 N (~ 141.4 N)
IV. 20√5 N (~ 44.7 N)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Horizontal pulling force (θ = 0°)): F = μ mg = 0.5 × 100 = 50 N. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Minimum pulling force at optimal angle θ = tan^-1(0.5)): F_min = μ mg / √(1 + μ^2) = 50 / √(1.25) = 100 / √5 = 20√5 N. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Pulling force required at angle θ = 45° above the horizontal): F cos 45° = μ (mg - F sin 45°) -> F / √2 = 0.5(100 - F/√2) -> 1.5 F / √2 = 50 -> F = 100√2 / 3 N. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Pushing force required at angle θ = 45° below the horizontal): F cos 45° = μ (mg + F sin 45°) -> F / √2 = 0.5(100 + F/√2) -> 0.5 F / √2 = 50 -> F = 100√2 N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block of mass m = 4 kg is pressed against a vertical rough wall by applying a horizontal force F (μ_s = 0.5, μ_k = 0.4, g = 10 m/s^2). Match each scenario in List I with the resulting value in List II:
List I:
A. Friction force when F = 100 N (block held stationary)
B. Friction force when F = 60 N (block slips downward)
C. Friction force when F = 40 N (block slips downward)
D. Minimum horizontal force required to prevent block from slipping
List II:
I. 24 N upward (kinetic)
II. 16 N upward (kinetic)
III. 80 N
IV. 40 N upward (static)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Friction force when F = 100 N (block held stationary)): Weight mg = 40 N. Limiting friction = 0.5 × 100 = 50 N. Since 40 N < 50 N, static friction = 40 N upward. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Friction force when F = 60 N (block slips downward)): Limiting friction = 0.5 × 60 = 30 N < 40 N, so block slips. Kinetic friction = μ_k F = 0.4 × 60 = 24 N upward. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Friction force when F = 40 N (block slips downward)): Kinetic friction = μ_k F = 0.4 × 40 = 16 N upward. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Minimum horizontal force required to prevent block from slipping): μ_s F ≥ mg -> 0.5 F = 40 -> F = 80 N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block of mass m = 5 kg is on an inclined plane of angle θ = 37° (sin 37° = 0.6, cos 37° = 0.8) with friction coefficient μ = 0.5 (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each force applied along the incline in List I with the description/value in List II:
List I:
A. Minimum upward force along incline to prevent block from sliding down
B. Minimum upward force along incline to start moving block upward
C. Friction force acting on block when an upward force of 30 N is applied
D. Acceleration down the incline when no external force is applied
List II:
I. 50 N
II. 2 m/s^2
III. 10 N
IV. 0 N
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Minimum upward force along incline to prevent block from sliding down): mg sin 37° = 30 N, f_max = μ mg cos 37° = 0.5 × 40 = 20 N. F_min = 30 - 20 = 10 N. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Minimum upward force along incline to start moving block upward): F_up = mg sin 37° + f_max = 30 + 20 = 50 N. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Friction force acting on block when an upward force of 30 N is applied): Applied force exactly balances gravity downhill component (30 N), so friction is 0 N. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Acceleration down the incline when no external force is applied): Net force = 30 - 20 = 10 N down incline; a = 10 / 5 = 2 m/s^2. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Two blocks A (mass 2 kg) and B (mass 4 kg) are stacked with A on top of B on a frictionless horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between A and B is μ = 0.3 (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each applied force case in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum acceleration without slipping when force is applied to block A
B. Maximum horizontal force applied to block A for both to move together
C. Maximum acceleration without slipping when force is applied to block B
D. Maximum horizontal force applied to block B for both to move together
List II:
I. 3 m/s^2
II. 1.5 m/s^2
III. 18 N
IV. 9 N
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum acceleration without slipping when force is applied to block A): f_max = μ m_A g = 0.3 × 20 = 6 N. Max acceleration of B is a_max = f_max / m_B = 6 / 4 = 1.5 m/s^2. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum horizontal force applied to block A for both to move together): F_max,A = (m_A + m_B) a_max = (2 + 4) × 1.5 = 9 N. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Maximum acceleration without slipping when force is applied to block B): Max acceleration of A is a_max = f_max / m_A = 6 / 2 = 3 m/s^2. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Maximum horizontal force applied to block B for both to move together): F_max,B = (m_A + m_B) a_max = 6 × 3 = 18 N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A coin of mass m is placed on a horizontal turntable at a distance r from the central rotation axis with coefficient of static friction μ. Match each condition in List I with its formula/value in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum angular speed ω_max without slipping at radius r
B. Maximum radial distance r_max for a given angular speed ω
C. Factor by which ω_max changes if radius r is doubled
D. Static friction force when rotating at half of maximum speed (ω = ω_max / 2)
List II:
I. μ g / ω^2
II. μ mg / 4
III. √(μ g / r)
IV. 1/√2 (~ 0.707)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum angular speed ω_max without slipping at radius r): Centripetal force m ω^2 r ≤ μ m g -> ω_max = √(μ g / r). Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum radial distance r_max for a given angular speed ω): r ≤ μ g / ω^2. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Factor by which ω_max changes if radius r is doubled): ω_max ∝ 1/√r, so doubling r scales ω_max by 1/√2. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Static friction force when rotating at half of maximum speed (ω = ω_max / 2)): f = m ω^2 r = m (ω_max/2)^2 r = (1/4) m ω_max^2 r = μ mg / 4. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A car of mass 1000 kg travels on a circular curve of radius R = 50 m (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each speed or friction quantity in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum speed on an unbanked flat road with μ_s = 0.5 without skidding
B. Optimum speed on a road banked at 45° where zero friction is required
C. Friction force on the flat road when traveling at v = 10 m/s
D. Maximum available limiting friction force on the flat road (μ_s = 0.5)
List II:
I. 2000 N
II. 10√5 m/s (~ 22.4 m/s)
III. 5000 N
IV. 5√10 m/s (~ 15.8 m/s)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum speed on an unbanked flat road with μ_s = 0.5 without skidding): v_max = √(μ_s g R) = √(0.5 × 10 × 50) = √250 = 5√10 m/s. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Optimum speed on a road banked at 45° where zero friction is required): v_banked = √(g R tan 45°) = √(10 × 50 × 1) = √500 = 10√5 m/s. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Friction force on the flat road when traveling at v = 10 m/s): f = m v^2 / R = 1000 × 100 / 50 = 2000 N. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Maximum available limiting friction force on the flat road (μ_s = 0.5)): f_max = μ_s m g = 0.5 × 1000 × 10 = 5000 N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block is projected up a rough incline of angle θ with initial speed u (coefficient of kinetic friction μ, with tan θ > μ). Match each kinematic quantity in List I with its formula in List II:
List I:
A. Retardation during upward motion (a_up)
B. Acceleration during downward return motion (a_down)
C. Ratio of time of descent to time of ascent (t_down / t_up)
D. Speed of the block upon returning to the launch point
List II:
I. g (sin θ + μ cos θ)
II. u √((sin θ - μ cos θ) / (sin θ + μ cos θ))
III. g (sin θ - μ cos θ)
IV. √((sin θ + μ cos θ) / (sin θ - μ cos θ))
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Retardation during upward motion (a_up)): Both gravity component and friction oppose upward motion: a_up = g(sin θ + μ cos θ). Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Acceleration during downward return motion (a_down)): Gravity pulls down while friction opposes downward motion: a_down = g(sin θ - μ cos θ). Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Ratio of time of descent to time of ascent (t_down / t_up)): Since s = (1/2) a t^2, t ∝ 1/√a, so t_down / t_up = √(a_up / a_down). Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Speed of the block upon returning to the launch point): v^2 = 2 a_down s and u^2 = 2 a_up s gives v = u √(a_down / a_up). Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A conveyor belt moves horizontally at constant speed v = 4 m/s. A package of mass m = 2 kg is placed gently on it with zero initial velocity (μ_k = 0.2, g = 10 m/s^2). Match the physical quantities in List I with their values in List II:
List I:
A. Time duration during which the package slips on the belt
B. Distance traveled by the package relative to ground during slipping
C. Work done by the motor driving the conveyor belt during slipping
D. Kinetic energy gained by the package
List II:
I. 32 J
II. 2 s
III. 16 J
IV. 4 m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Time duration during which the package slips on the belt): Acceleration a = μ_k g = 0.2 × 10 = 2 m/s^2. Time to match belt speed t = v / a = 4 / 2 = 2 s. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Distance traveled by the package relative to ground during slipping): s_pkg = v^2 / (2a) = 16 / 4 = 4 m. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Work done by the motor driving the conveyor belt during slipping): Belt moves distance s_belt = v t = 4 × 2 = 8 m. Work done = f_k × s_belt = (0.2 × 20) × 8 = 4 × 8 = 32 J. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Kinetic energy gained by the package): KE = (1/2) m v^2 = (1/2)(2)(16) = 16 J (the other 16 J dissipates as heat). Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Block A (mass 2 kg) rests on Block B (mass 3 kg), which rests on a rough horizontal floor (μ_1 = 0.4 between A and B, μ_2 = 0.2 with floor, g = 10 m/s^2). A horizontal force F is applied to lower block B. Match the applied force F in List I with the resulting accelerations in List II:
List I:
A. F = 8 N applied to block B
B. F = 20 N applied to block B
C. F = 30 N applied to block B
D. F = 42 N applied to block B
List II:
I. a_A = 2 m/s^2, a_B = 2 m/s^2 (moving together)
II. a_A = 4 m/s^2, a_B = 8 m/s^2 (relative slipping occurs)
III. a_A = 0 m/s^2, a_B = 0 m/s^2 (system at rest)
IV. a_A = 4 m/s^2, a_B = 4 m/s^2 (verge of relative slipping)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (F = 8 N applied to block B): Limiting friction with floor = 0.2 × (2 + 3) × 10 = 10 N. Since F = 8 N < 10 N, system remains at rest. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (F = 20 N applied to block B): Limiting friction between A and B is 0.4 × 20 = 8 N, allowing max acceleration of A = 4 m/s^2. For F = 20 N, common acceleration is (20 - 10)/5 = 2 m/s^2 < 4 m/s^2, so they move together. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (F = 30 N applied to block B): Common acceleration = (30 - 10)/5 = 4 m/s^2, exactly the maximum acceleration A can sustain without slipping. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (F = 42 N applied to block B): Since F > 30 N, relative slipping occurs. Friction on A is 8 N -> a_A = 8/2 = 4 m/s^2. Net force on B = 42 - 8 - 10 = 24 N -> a_B = 24/3 = 8 m/s^2. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
In the same system (m_A = 2 kg on m_B = 3 kg on rough floor with μ_1 = 0.4 between blocks, μ_2 = 0.2 with floor, g = 10 m/s^2), a horizontal force F is now applied to top block A. Match each applied force in List I with the outcome in List II:
List I:
A. F = 6 N applied to block A
B. F = 16 N applied to block A
C. F = 24 N applied to block A
D. Minimum force on block A required to cause motion of block B
List II:
I. Block A accelerates at 8 m/s^2 while block B remains at rest
II. Block A accelerates at 4 m/s^2 while block B remains at rest
III. Impossible (Block B will never move)
IV. Both blocks remain at rest (a_A = 0, a_B = 0)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (F = 6 N applied to block A): Limiting friction between A and B is 8 N. Since F = 6 N < 8 N, A does not slip on B, and max force on floor (6 N) < 10 N, so neither moves. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (F = 16 N applied to block A): F > 8 N, so A slips. Friction on A is 8 N -> a_A = (16 - 8)/2 = 4 m/s^2. Force transmitted to B is 8 N < 10 N (floor friction), so B remains at rest. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (F = 24 N applied to block A): A slips with 8 N friction -> a_A = (24 - 8)/2 = 8 m/s^2. Force transmitted to B is still 8 N < 10 N, so B remains at rest. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Minimum force on block A required to cause motion of block B): The maximum friction force that A can exert on B is 8 N, which is strictly less than the 10 N needed to overcome floor friction. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block of mass m is placed on a rough wedge of inclination angle θ = 45° with coefficient of static friction μ = 0.5. The wedge is accelerated horizontally with acceleration a (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each condition in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Minimum horizontal acceleration to prevent slipping down
B. Maximum horizontal acceleration before block slips up the incline
C. Horizontal acceleration at which friction force is strictly zero
D. Normal reaction on the block when a = 10 m/s^2
List II:
I. 10 m/s^2
II. 10/3 m/s^2
III. 10√2 m N (or √2 mg)
IV. 30 m/s^2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Minimum horizontal acceleration to prevent slipping down): a_min = g (sin 45° - μ cos 45°) / (cos 45° + μ sin 45°) = 10 (1 - 0.5) / (1 + 0.5) = 10 / 3 m/s^2. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum horizontal acceleration before block slips up the incline): a_max = g (sin 45° + μ cos 45°) / (cos 45° - μ sin 45°) = 10 (1 + 0.5) / (1 - 0.5) = 30 m/s^2. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Horizontal acceleration at which friction force is strictly zero): Zero friction requires a_0 = g tan 45° = 10 × 1 = 10 m/s^2. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Normal reaction on the block when a = 10 m/s^2): N = m (g cos 45° + a sin 45°) = m (10/√2 + 10/√2) = 10√2 m N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A heavy cable is wrapped around a rough fixed horizontal cylinder by total contact angle θ with friction coefficient μ. Match each configuration in List I with the tension ratio T_2 / T_1 in List II (Capstan equation):
List I:
A. Wrapped by half a turn (θ = π rad) with μ = 0.2
B. Wrapped by one full turn (θ = 2π rad) with μ = 0.2
C. Wrapped by two full turns (θ = 4π rad) with μ = 0.2
D. General Capstan formula for tension amplification ratio
List II:
I. e^(0.4π) (~ 3.51)
II. e^(μ θ)
III. e^(0.2π) (~ 1.87)
IV. e^(0.8π) (~ 12.34)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Wrapped by half a turn (θ = π rad) with μ = 0.2): T_2 / T_1 = e^(μ θ) = e^(0.2 × π) ≈ 1.87. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Wrapped by one full turn (θ = 2π rad) with μ = 0.2): T_2 / T_1 = e^(0.2 × 2π) = e^(0.4π) ≈ 3.51. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Wrapped by two full turns (θ = 4π rad) with μ = 0.2): T_2 / T_1 = e^(0.2 × 4π) = e^(0.8π) ≈ 12.34. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (General Capstan formula for tension amplification ratio): Integration of dT / T = μ dθ yields the exponential tension ratio e^(μ θ). Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
An insect of mass m = 0.1 kg crawls slowly up the inside of a rough hemispherical bowl of radius R = 1 m with friction coefficient μ = 0.75 (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each parameter in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum angle θ from the lowest point the insect can reach
B. Maximum vertical height reached above the bottom of the bowl
C. Maximum horizontal distance from the vertical axis of symmetry
D. Normal force exerted by the bowl on the insect at the highest point
List II:
I. 0.6 m (60 cm)
II. tan^-1(0.75) (~ 37°)
III. 0.8 N
IV. 0.2 m (20 cm)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum angle θ from the lowest point the insect can reach): At limiting equilibrium, mg sin θ = μ mg cos θ -> tan θ = μ = 0.75 = 3/4. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum vertical height reached above the bottom of the bowl): h = R (1 - cos θ) = 1 × (1 - 4/5) = 0.2 m. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Maximum horizontal distance from the vertical axis of symmetry): r = R sin θ = 1 × (3/5) = 0.6 m. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Normal force exerted by the bowl on the insect at the highest point): N = mg cos θ = (0.1 × 10) × (4/5) = 0.8 N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A rotor of radius R = 2 m spins about its vertical axis. A person of mass m = 50 kg leans against the rough inner wall with static friction coefficient μ_s = 0.5 (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each parameter in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Minimum angular velocity ω_min to prevent slipping down
B. Minimum normal reaction required from the wall
C. Actual vertical friction force when spinning at ω = 2√10 rad/s
D. Normal reaction force on the person when spinning at ω = 2√10 rad/s
List II:
I. 500 N
II. 1000 N
III. 4000 N
IV. √10 rad/s (~ 3.16 rad/s)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Minimum angular velocity ω_min to prevent slipping down): μ_s (m ω^2 R) ≥ mg -> ω ≥ √(g / (μ_s R)) = √(10 / (0.5 × 2)) = √10 rad/s. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Minimum normal reaction required from the wall): N_min = mg / μ_s = (50 × 10) / 0.5 = 1000 N. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Actual vertical friction force when spinning at ω = 2√10 rad/s): In static equilibrium the vertical friction force simply balances the weight: f = mg = 500 N. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Normal reaction force on the person when spinning at ω = 2√10 rad/s): N = m ω^2 R = 50 × (40) × 2 = 4000 N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A uniform horizontal rod of mass M = 3 kg and length L = 1 m rests symmetrically on two counter-rotating rough rollers separated by 2d = 0.6 m (d = 0.3 m). Both rollers have kinetic friction coefficient μ = 0.4 (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each oscillation parameter in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Effective restoring force constant k_eff
B. Restoring force on the rod when displaced by x = 5 cm (0.05 m)
C. Angular frequency ω_0 of resulting harmonic oscillations
D. Time period of the horizontal simple harmonic oscillations
List II:
I. 40 N/m
II. π√(3/10) s (~ 1.72 s)
III. 2 N
IV. 2√(10/3) rad/s (~ 3.65 rad/s)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Effective restoring force constant k_eff): Restoring force F = μ M g x / d -> k_eff = μ M g / d = (0.4 × 30) / 0.3 = 40 N/m. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Restoring force on the rod when displaced by x = 5 cm (0.05 m)): F = k_eff x = 40 × 0.05 = 2.0 N. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Angular frequency ω_0 of resulting harmonic oscillations): ω_0 = √(k_eff / M) = √(40 / 3) = 2√(10/3) rad/s. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Time period of the horizontal simple harmonic oscillations): T = 2π / ω_0 = 2π √(3/40) = π √(3/10) s. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block of mass m is projected with initial speed u = 6 m/s on a rough horizontal floor where the coefficient of friction varies as μ(x) = 0.2 x (take g = 10 m/s^2). Match each kinematic/dynamic parameter in List I with its value in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum distance traveled by the block before stopping
B. Speed of the block when it reaches x = 4 m
C. Maximum deceleration experienced by the block
D. Friction force on a 2 kg block at the stopping point
List II:
I. 6√2 m/s^2
II. 3√2 m (~ 4.24 m)
III. 12√2 N
IV. 2 m/s
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum distance traveled by the block before stopping): v dv/dx = -μ(x) g = -2x -> v^2 = u^2 - 2x^2 = 36 - 2x^2. Setting v = 0 gives x = √18 = 3√2 m. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Speed of the block when it reaches x = 4 m): v = √(36 - 2(16)) = √4 = 2 m/s. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Maximum deceleration experienced by the block): Max deceleration occurs at the stopping point: a_max = 2 x_max = 2 × 3√2 = 6√2 m/s^2. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Friction force on a 2 kg block at the stopping point): f = m a_max = 2 × 6√2 = 12√2 N. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A constant force F = (3i + 4j - 2k) N acts on a particle. Match the displacements in List I with the work done by the force in List II:
List I:
A. Displacement d1 = (2i + 3j + 1k) m
B. Displacement d2 = (2i + 0j + 3k) m
C. Displacement d3 = (4i - 1j + 2k) m
D. Displacement d4 = (-2i + 2j + 5k) m
List II:
I. 0 J
II. -8 J
III. 16 J
IV. 4 J
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Displacement d1 = (2i + 3j + 1k) m): W = F . d1 = 3(2) + 4(3) - 2(1) = 6 + 12 - 2 = 16 J. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Displacement d2 = (2i + 0j + 3k) m): W = F . d2 = 3(2) + 4(0) - 2(3) = 6 + 0 - 6 = 0 J. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Displacement d3 = (4i - 1j + 2k) m): W = F . d3 = 3(4) + 4(-1) - 2(2) = 12 - 4 - 4 = 4 J. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Displacement d4 = (-2i + 2j + 5k) m): W = F . d4 = 3(-2) + 4(2) - 2(5) = -6 + 8 - 10 = -8 J. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A linear spring of stiffness k = 200 N/m is attached to a block. Match the spring displacements from equilibrium (x = 0) in List I with the work done by the spring force in List II:
List I:
A. Stretching from x = 0 to x = +0.1 m
B. Stretching further from x = +0.1 m to x = +0.2 m
C. Releasing from compression x = -0.2 m to x = 0 m
D. Compressing from x = 0 to x = -0.05 m
List II:
I. -3.0 J
II. +4.0 J
III. -0.25 J
IV. -1.0 J
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Stretching from x = 0 to x = +0.1 m): Ws = (1/2)k(xi^2 - xf^2) = 0.5 * 200 * (0 - 0.01) = -1.0 J. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Stretching further from x = +0.1 m to x = +0.2 m): Ws = 0.5 * 200 * (0.01 - 0.04) = 100 * (-0.03) = -3.0 J. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Releasing from compression x = -0.2 m to x = 0 m): Ws = 0.5 * 200 * (0.04 - 0) = +4.0 J. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Compressing from x = 0 to x = -0.05 m): Ws = 0.5 * 200 * (0 - 0.0025) = -0.25 J. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match each potential energy function U(x) in List I with the nature of equilibrium of a particle at x = 0 in List II:
List I:
A. U(x) = U0 + (1/2) k x^2 (k > 0)
B. U(x) = U0 - (1/2) k x^2 (k > 0)
C. U(x) = U0 (constant for all x)
D. U(x) = U0 - F0 x (F0 != 0)
List II:
I. Neutral equilibrium
II. Stable equilibrium
III. Non-equilibrium (accelerating state)
IV. Unstable equilibrium
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (U(x) = U0 + (1/2) k x^2 (k > 0)): dU/dx = kx = 0 at x=0 and d^2U/dx^2 = k > 0, corresponding to a local potential energy minimum. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (U(x) = U0 - (1/2) k x^2 (k > 0)): dU/dx = -kx = 0 at x=0 and d^2U/dx^2 = -k < 0, corresponding to a local potential energy maximum. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (U(x) = U0 (constant for all x)): dU/dx = 0 and d^2U/dx^2 = 0 everywhere, so the particle remains in equilibrium upon displacement. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (U(x) = U0 - F0 x (F0 != 0)): dU/dx = -F0 != 0, so a constant net force acts on the particle preventing equilibrium. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the physical quantities related to work, energy, and power in List I with their SI units and dimensional formulas in List II:
List I:
A. Mechanical Work / Kinetic Energy
B. Instantaneous Power
C. Spring stiffness constant k
D. Linear momentum p
List II:
I. Joule (J) and [M L^2 T^(-2)]
II. kg m/s and [M L T^(-1)]
III. Watt (W) and [M L^2 T^(-3)]
IV. N/m and [M T^(-2)]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Mechanical Work / Kinetic Energy): Work is force times displacement: N * m = kg m^2 s^(-2), dimensions [M L^2 T^(-2)]. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Instantaneous Power): Power is rate of work: J/s = kg m^2 s^(-3), dimensions [M L^2 T^(-3)]. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Spring stiffness constant k): Stiffness k = Force/displacement: N/m = kg s^(-2), dimensions [M L^0 T^(-2)]. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Linear momentum p): Linear momentum is mass times velocity: kg m s^(-1), dimensions [M L T^(-1)]. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A variable force F(x) = (6x^2 - 4x + 2) N acts along the x-axis on a 2 kg body. Match the displacement intervals in List I with the work done by F in List II:
List I:
A. From x = 0 m to x = 1 m
B. From x = 0 m to x = 2 m
C. From x = 1 m to x = 3 m
D. From x = -1 m to x = 1 m
List II:
I. 12 J
II. 8 J
III. 2 J
IV. 40 J
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (From x = 0 m to x = 1 m): Integral of (6x^2 - 4x + 2)dx is [2x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x]. Evaluated from 0 to 1 gives 2 - 2 + 2 = 2 J. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (From x = 0 m to x = 2 m): Evaluated from 0 to 2 gives 2(8) - 2(4) + 2(2) = 16 - 8 + 4 = 12 J. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (From x = 1 m to x = 3 m): At x=3: 2(27) - 2(9) + 2(3) = 54 - 18 + 6 = 42 J. Subtracting value at x=1 (2 J) gives 40 J. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (From x = -1 m to x = 1 m): At x=-1: 2(-1) - 2(1) + 2(-1) = -6 J. Value at x=1 is 2 J. Work = 2 - (-6) = 8 J. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A particle of mass m is tied to a light string of length L and whirls in a vertical circle. Match the parameters at critical threshold in List I with their exact values in List II:
List I:
A. Minimum speed at lowest point to complete full circle
B. Speed at highest point when launched with critical speed sqrt(5gL)
C. Speed when string is horizontal when launched with sqrt(5gL)
D. Difference between lowest and highest string tensions (T_low - T_high)
List II:
I. sqrt(gL)
II. sqrt(3gL)
III. 6mg
IV. sqrt(5gL)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Minimum speed at lowest point to complete full circle): At top, mg provides centripetal force: v_top = sqrt(gL). By conservation of energy, u = sqrt(gL + 4gL) = sqrt(5gL). Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Speed at highest point when launched with critical speed sqrt(5gL)): Energy conservation: (1/2)m u^2 = (1/2)m v_top^2 + 2mgL gives v_top = sqrt(5gL - 4gL) = sqrt(gL). Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Speed when string is horizontal when launched with sqrt(5gL)): Energy conservation: (1/2)m u^2 = (1/2)m v_horiz^2 + mgL gives v_horiz = sqrt(5gL - 2gL) = sqrt(3gL). Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Difference between lowest and highest string tensions (T_low - T_high)): T_low = mg + m(5gL)/L = 6mg; T_high = m(gL)/L - mg = 0; thus T_low - T_high = 6mg. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
The interatomic potential energy between two atoms is modeled by U(r) = U0 * [(r0/r)^12 - 2*(r0/r)^6]. Match the physical properties in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Equilibrium separation where net force is zero
B. Depth of the potential well (dissociation/binding energy)
C. Separation distance r at which potential energy U(r) = 0
D. Effective harmonic force constant k_eff for small oscillations about r0
List II:
I. r0 / 2^(1/6)
II. r0
III. 72 * U0 / r0^2
IV. U0
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Equilibrium separation where net force is zero): dU/dr = U0 * [-12 r0^12 / r^13 + 12 r0^6 / r^7] = 0 implies r^6 = r0^6, so r = r0. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Depth of the potential well (dissociation/binding energy)): U(r0) = U0 * [1 - 2] = -U0. The binding energy required to separate atoms to infinity is U0. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Separation distance r at which potential energy U(r) = 0): Setting (r0/r)^12 - 2(r0/r)^6 = 0 yields (r0/r)^6 = 2, so r = r0 / 2^(1/6). Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Effective harmonic force constant k_eff for small oscillations about r0): d^2U/dr^2 at r0: U0 * [156/r0^2 - 84/r0^2] = 72 U0 / r0^2. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A vehicle of mass m starts from rest and is driven by an engine delivering constant mechanical power P0. Match the kinematic quantities in List I with their proportionalities in List II:
List I:
A. Speed as a function of time, v(t)
B. Displacement as a function of time, x(t)
C. Acceleration as a function of time, a(t)
D. Tractive driving force as a function of speed, F(v)
List II:
I. proportional to t^(1/2)
II. proportional to v^(-1)
III. proportional to t^(3/2)
IV. proportional to t^(-1/2)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Speed as a function of time, v(t)): P0 = d/dt (1/2 m v^2) => (1/2) m v^2 = P0 t => v(t) = sqrt(2 P0 t / m) proportional to t^(1/2). Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Displacement as a function of time, x(t)): Integrating v(t) dt gives x(t) = (2/3) sqrt(2 P0 / m) t^(3/2) proportional to t^(3/2). Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Acceleration as a function of time, a(t)): Differentiating v(t) gives a(t) = sqrt(P0 / (2m t)) proportional to t^(-1/2). Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Tractive driving force as a function of speed, F(v)): Since Power P0 = F * v, driving force is F = P0 / v proportional to v^(-1). Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match each physical scenario in List I with the work done by the specified force in List II:
List I:
A. Kinetic friction on a block sliding to rest on a fixed rough horizontal floor
B. Static friction on the driving wheels of a car accelerating forward without slip
C. Normal reaction on a block sliding down a fixed smooth inclined plane
D. Gravitational force on a projectile during upward flight to maximum height h
List II:
I. Positive work increasing translational kinetic energy
II. Negative work equal to -m g h
III. Negative work dissipating mechanical energy into thermal energy
IV. Zero work because force is perpendicular to displacement
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Kinetic friction on a block sliding to rest on a fixed rough horizontal floor): Kinetic friction opposes sliding displacement (theta = 180 deg), doing negative work -f_k * d and generating heat. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Static friction on the driving wheels of a car accelerating forward without slip): Static friction at the road contact acts in the direction of vehicle acceleration, doing positive work on the car. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Normal reaction on a block sliding down a fixed smooth inclined plane): The normal contact force is always normal to the inclined surface (theta = 90 deg), so W = N . d = 0. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Gravitational force on a projectile during upward flight to maximum height h): Gravity acts downward while displacement is upward (theta = 180 deg), so work done is -m g h. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Consider vertical circular motion for a particle of mass m attached to a light rigid rod of length R versus a light inextensible string of length R. Match the quantities in List I with their values in List II:
List I:
A. Minimum speed at bottom for rod system to reach the top
B. Minimum speed at bottom for string system to complete full circle
C. Tension in rod at highest point when launched with u = 2*sqrt(gR)
D. Tension in string at lowest point when launched with critical speed sqrt(5gR)
List II:
I. sqrt(5gR)
II. Zero
III. 6mg
IV. 2*sqrt(gR)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Minimum speed at bottom for rod system to reach the top): A rigid rod can support compression, so velocity at top can be 0. (1/2)m u^2 = mg(2R) => u = sqrt(4gR) = 2*sqrt(gR). Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Minimum speed at bottom for string system to complete full circle): A string requires tension T >= 0 at top, demanding v_top >= sqrt(gR). Energy conservation gives u = sqrt(5gR). Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Tension in rod at highest point when launched with u = 2*sqrt(gR)): At the top v = 0, so centripetal acceleration is zero. Radial equilibrium gives T + mg = 0? Actually normal thrust N = mg, so tension is zero. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Tension in string at lowest point when launched with critical speed sqrt(5gR)): T_bottom = mg + m u^2 / R = mg + m(5gR)/R = 6mg. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Two blocks of masses m1 = 2 kg and m2 = 3 kg lie on a frictionless horizontal table connected by a spring of stiffness k = 600 N/m. The spring is compressed by 0.1 m and released from rest. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Total initial potential energy stored in the spring
B. Kinetic energy of block m1 when spring reaches natural length
C. Kinetic energy of block m2 when spring reaches natural length
D. Maximum speed attained by the center of mass of the two-block system
List II:
I. 1.2 J
II. 3.0 J
III. 0 m/s
IV. 1.8 J
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Total initial potential energy stored in the spring): U = (1/2) k x0^2 = 0.5 * 600 * (0.1)^2 = 3.0 J. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Kinetic energy of block m1 when spring reaches natural length): Momentum conservation gives p1 = p2. K1/K2 = m2/m1 = 3/2. Thus K1 = (3/5) * 3.0 J = 1.8 J. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Kinetic energy of block m2 when spring reaches natural length): Since K1 + K2 = 3.0 J, K2 = (2/5) * 3.0 J = 1.2 J. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Maximum speed attained by the center of mass of the two-block system): No external horizontal forces act on the system, so the velocity of the center of mass remains zero throughout. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match each 2D force field F(x, y) in List I with its physical characteristic and potential energy function U(x, y) (with reference U(0,0)=0) in List II:
List I:
A. F = (2xy) i + (x^2) j
B. F = y i - x j
C. F = (3x^2) i + (4y^3) j
D. F = -k(x i + y j)
List II:
I. Conservative with U(x,y) = -x^2 y
II. Conservative central force with U(r) = (1/2) k r^2
III. Non-conservative with non-zero curl
IV. Conservative with U(x,y) = -(x^3 + y^4)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (F = (2xy) i + (x^2) j): Curl F = d/dx(x^2) - d/dy(2xy) = 2x - 2x = 0. Force is conservative; U = -integral (2xy dx + x^2 dy) = -x^2 y. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (F = y i - x j): Curl F = d/dx(-x) - d/dy(y) = -1 - 1 = -2 k != 0. The force is non-conservative and cannot have a scalar potential. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (F = (3x^2) i + (4y^3) j): Curl F = 0. Integrating -F . dr gives U(x,y) = -x^3 - y^4. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (F = -k(x i + y j)): Curl F = 0. The force is isotropic and directed towards origin; U(r) = (1/2) k (x^2 + y^2) = (1/2) k r^2. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A small particle of mass m rests at the apex of a fixed smooth sphere of radius R. Given an infinitesimal nudge, it slides down. Match the quantities at zenith angle theta in List I with their values in List II:
List I:
A. Speed of the particle as a function of angle theta
B. Normal reaction force N(theta) exerted by sphere on particle
C. Cosine of the critical angle at which the particle detaches from sphere
D. Height above the horizontal base where the particle loses contact
List II:
I. mg(3 cos theta - 2)
II. (5/3) R
III. sqrt(2gR(1 - cos theta))
IV. 2/3
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Speed of the particle as a function of angle theta): From energy conservation: (1/2)m v^2 = mgR(1 - cos theta) => v = sqrt(2gR(1 - cos theta)). Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Normal reaction force N(theta) exerted by sphere on particle): Radial equation: mg cos theta - N = m v^2 / R = 2mg(1 - cos theta) => N = mg(3 cos theta - 2). Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Cosine of the critical angle at which the particle detaches from sphere): Detachment occurs when normal reaction vanishes: N = 0 => 3 cos theta_c - 2 = 0 => cos theta_c = 2/3. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Height above the horizontal base where the particle loses contact): Height from center is R cos theta_c = (2/3)R. Total height from sphere base is R + (2/3)R = (5/3)R. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A particle of mass m moves along the x-axis in a potential well given by U(x) = (a/2) x^2 - (b/4) x^4, where a, b > 0. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Positions of unstable equilibrium points
B. Angular frequency of small oscillations about the stable origin x = 0
C. Height of the potential barrier (energy required to escape from well)
D. Value of the restoring force at small displacement x << sqrt(a/b)
List II:
I. sqrt(a/m)
II. a^2 / (4b)
III. -a x
IV. x = +- sqrt(a/b)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Positions of unstable equilibrium points): dU/dx = ax - bx^3 = x(a - bx^2) = 0. Points x = +-sqrt(a/b) have d^2U/dx^2 = a - 3b(a/b) = -2a < 0 (unstable maxima). Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Angular frequency of small oscillations about the stable origin x = 0): At x = 0, d^2U/dx^2 = a > 0 (stable minimum). The small oscillation frequency is omega = sqrt(U''(0)/m) = sqrt(a/m). Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Height of the potential barrier (energy required to escape from well)): Potential barrier is U(+-sqrt(a/b)) - U(0) = (a/2)(a/b) - (b/4)(a^2/b^2) = a^2/(2b) - a^2/(4b) = a^2/(4b). Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Value of the restoring force at small displacement x << sqrt(a/b)): Restoring force F(x) = -dU/dx = -ax + bx^3. For x << sqrt(a/b), bx^3 is negligible, leaving F approx -ax. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A block of mass m is attached to the lower end of a vertical spring of stiffness k. Initially, the spring is at its natural length and the block is released from rest. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Extension of the spring at the equilibrium position
B. Maximum extension of the spring below the release point
C. Maximum speed achieved by the falling block
D. Work done by gravity during displacement from release to maximum extension
List II:
I. g * sqrt(m / k)
II. mg / k
III. 2m^2 g^2 / k
IV. 2mg / k
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Extension of the spring at the equilibrium position): At equilibrium, upward spring force balances gravity: k x_eq = mg => x_eq = mg / k. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum extension of the spring below the release point): By energy conservation: mg x_max = (1/2) k x_max^2 => x_max = 2mg / k. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Maximum speed achieved by the falling block): Maximum speed occurs at equilibrium x = mg/k: (1/2)m v_max^2 = mg(mg/k) - (1/2)k(mg/k)^2 = (1/2)m^2 g^2 / k => v_max = g sqrt(m/k). Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Work done by gravity during displacement from release to maximum extension): Wg = mg * x_max = mg * (2mg/k) = 2m^2 g^2 / k. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A body of mass m enters a resistive fluid medium at x = 0 with speed v0, experiencing a drag force F = -k v^2. Match the kinematic expressions in List I with List II:
List I:
A. Speed as a function of distance travelled, v(x)
B. Speed as a function of time elapsed, v(t)
C. Displacement as a function of time, x(t)
D. Total work done by the resistive drag force as t -> infinity
List II:
I. v0 * exp(-k x / m)
II. -(1/2) m v0^2
III. v0 / (1 + (k v0 / m) t)
IV. (m/k) * ln(1 + (k v0 / m) t)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Speed as a function of distance travelled, v(x)): m v dv/dx = -k v^2 => dv/v = -(k/m) dx. Integrating gives ln(v/v0) = -kx/m => v(x) = v0 exp(-kx/m). Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Speed as a function of time elapsed, v(t)): m dv/dt = -k v^2 => -dv/v^2 = (k/m) dt. Integrating gives 1/v - 1/v0 = (k/m)t => v(t) = v0 / (1 + k v0 t / m). Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Displacement as a function of time, x(t)): x(t) = integral v(t) dt = integral [v0 / (1 + k v0 t / m)] dt = (m/k) ln(1 + k v0 t / m). Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Total work done by the resistive drag force as t -> infinity): By the work-energy theorem, W_drag = K_final - K_initial = 0 - (1/2) m v0^2 = -(1/2) m v0^2. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A particle of mass m is whirled in a vertical circle of radius R with bottom speed u = sqrt(4gR). Match the parameters at and after string slackening in List I with List II:
List I:
A. Cosine of angle theta from upward vertical where string slacks (T = 0)
B. Speed of the particle at the instant string slacks
C. Vertical height of the particle above the lowest launch point when string slacks
D. Maximum extra vertical height achieved as a projectile after slacking
List II:
I. sqrt((2/3) gR)
II. (5/27) R
III. 2/3
IV. (5/3) R
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Cosine of angle theta from upward vertical where string slacks (T = 0)): Speed v^2 = u^2 - 2gR(1 + cos theta_up). Radial eq: T + mg cos theta_up = m v^2 / R. For T=0: 3 cos theta_up = (u^2 - 2gR)/(gR) = 2 => cos theta_up = 2/3. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Speed of the particle at the instant string slacks): v_s^2 = gR cos theta_up = (2/3) gR => v_s = sqrt((2/3) gR). Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Vertical height of the particle above the lowest launch point when string slacks): Height from lowest point is R + R cos theta_up = R(1 + 2/3) = (5/3) R. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Maximum extra vertical height achieved as a projectile after slacking): Vertical projectile speed is v_s sin theta_up. Extra height h = (v_s sin theta_up)^2 / (2g) = ((2/3)gR * (1 - 4/9)) / (2g) = (5/27) R. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A uniform flexible rope of mass M and length L lies on a frictionless horizontal table with 1/n-th of its length hanging over the edge. It is released from rest. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Initial gravitational potential energy (table top as reference U = 0)
B. Gravitational potential energy when the entire rope just slips off the table
C. Speed of the rope at the instant the last link slips off the table
D. Total work done by gravity during the slipping process
List II:
I. -M g L / 2
II. sqrt(gL * (1 - 1/n^2))
III. (M g L / 2) * (1 - 1/n^2)
IV. -M g L / (2 n^2)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Initial gravitational potential energy (table top as reference U = 0)): Hanging mass is M/n with center of mass at depth L/(2n). U_i = -(M/n) g (L/(2n)) = -MgL / (2n^2). Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Gravitational potential energy when the entire rope just slips off the table): When fully vertical, center of mass of the entire rope of mass M is at depth L/2. U_f = -MgL / 2. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Speed of the rope at the instant the last link slips off the table): By energy conservation: (1/2) M v^2 = U_i - U_f = (MgL/2)(1 - 1/n^2) => v = sqrt(gL(1 - 1/n^2)). Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Total work done by gravity during the slipping process): Work done by gravity is -(U_f - U_i) = (MgL/2) - (MgL / 2n^2) = (MgL/2)(1 - 1/n^2). Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A vehicle of mass m accelerates from rest along a straight horizontal track. Its engine delivers power proportional to instantaneous speed: P(v) = c * v, where c is a constant. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Tractive driving force exerted on the vehicle
B. Acceleration of the vehicle
C. Speed of the vehicle after covering a distance s from rest
D. Time required for the vehicle to attain a speed v1 from rest
List II:
I. sqrt(2 c s / m)
II. Constant force c
III. m * v1 / c
IV. Constant acceleration c / m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Tractive driving force exerted on the vehicle): Power P = F * v => c * v = F * v => F = c (constant force independent of speed). Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Acceleration of the vehicle): By Newton's second law, a = F / m = c / m, which is constant in time. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Speed of the vehicle after covering a distance s from rest): Using v^2 = 2 a s for constant acceleration gives v(s) = sqrt(2 (c/m) s) = sqrt(2 c s / m). Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Time required for the vehicle to attain a speed v1 from rest): Using v1 = a t gives t = v1 / a = v1 / (c/m) = m v1 / c. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A particle of mass m moves in a central potential U_eff(r) = (k/2) r^2 + L0^2 / (2 m r^2), where L0 is constant angular momentum and k > 0. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Radius r0 of the stable circular orbit (minimum of effective potential)
B. Minimum value of the effective potential energy U_eff(r0)
C. Second derivative d^2 U_eff / dr^2 evaluated at r = r0
D. Angular frequency omega_r of small radial oscillations about r0
List II:
I. (L0^2 / (m k))^(1/4)
II. 2 * sqrt(k / m)
III. L0 * sqrt(k / m)
IV. 4k
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Radius r0 of the stable circular orbit (minimum of effective potential)): dU_eff/dr = kr - L0^2/(m r^3) = 0 => kr^4 = L0^2/m => r0 = (L0^2 / (mk))^(1/4). Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Minimum value of the effective potential energy U_eff(r0)): Substitute r0^2 = L0/sqrt(mk): U_eff = (k/2)(L0/sqrt(mk)) + (L0^2/(2m))(sqrt(mk)/L0) = L0 sqrt(k/m). Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Second derivative d^2 U_eff / dr^2 evaluated at r = r0): d^2U/dr^2 = k + 3 L0^2 / (m r0^4) = k + 3 L0^2 / (m (L0^2/mk)) = k + 3k = 4k. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Angular frequency omega_r of small radial oscillations about r0): omega_r = sqrt(U_eff''(r0) / m) = sqrt(4k / m) = 2 sqrt(k/m). Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the uniform rigid bodies of mass M and radius R in List I with their moments of inertia about the specified symmetry axis in List II:
List I:
A. Thin circular ring about central axis perpendicular to its plane
B. Uniform circular disc about central axis perpendicular to its plane
C. Uniform solid sphere about any diametrical axis
D. Thin spherical shell about any diametrical axis
List II:
I. (1/2) M R^2
II. (2/3) M R^2
III. M R^2
IV. (2/5) M R^2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Thin circular ring about central axis perpendicular to its plane): All mass elements are at distance R from the central axis: I = integral r^2 dm = M R^2. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Uniform circular disc about central axis perpendicular to its plane): Integrating concentric rings gives I = integral (r^2)(2 pi r sigma dr) = (1/2) M R^2. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Uniform solid sphere about any diametrical axis): Integrating concentric spherical shells or thin circular discs yields I = (2/5) M R^2. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Thin spherical shell about any diametrical axis): Integrating over the spherical surface gives I = (2/3) M R^2. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the rigid bodies in List I with their moments of inertia obtained via parallel or perpendicular axis theorems in List II:
List I:
A. Uniform circular disc (mass M, radius R) about a diameter in its plane
B. Uniform circular disc (mass M, radius R) about a tangent line in its plane
C. Thin uniform rod (mass M, length L) about an axis through one end perpendicular to rod
D. Thin uniform rod (mass M, length L) about an axis through center perpendicular to rod
List II:
I. (5/4) M R^2
II. (1/3) M L^2
III. (1/12) M L^2
IV. (1/4) M R^2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Uniform circular disc (mass M, radius R) about a diameter in its plane): Perpendicular axis theorem: Ix + Iy = Iz = (1/2)MR^2. By symmetry Ix = Iy = (1/4) M R^2. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Uniform circular disc (mass M, radius R) about a tangent line in its plane): Parallel axis theorem: I_tan = I_dia + M R^2 = (1/4)MR^2 + MR^2 = (5/4) M R^2. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Thin uniform rod (mass M, length L) about an axis through one end perpendicular to rod): Parallel axis theorem: I_end = I_cm + M(L/2)^2 = (1/12)ML^2 + (1/4)ML^2 = (1/3) M L^2. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Thin uniform rod (mass M, length L) about an axis through center perpendicular to rod): Direct integration: integral_{-L/2}^{L/2} x^2 (M/L) dx = (1/12) M L^2. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A constant force F = (2i + 3j - 1k) N acts at various points r. Match each position vector r in List I with the resulting torque tau = r x F about the origin in List II:
List I:
A. Position vector r1 = (1i + 0j + 0k) m
B. Position vector r2 = (0i + 1j + 0k) m
C. Position vector r3 = (0i + 0j + 1k) m
D. Position vector r4 = (1i + 1j + 0k) m
List II:
I. (-3i + 2j) N m
II. (1j + 3k) N m
III. (-1i + 1j + 1k) N m
IV. (-1i - 2k) N m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Position vector r1 = (1i + 0j + 0k) m): tau = i x (2i + 3j - k) = 3(i x j) - 1(i x k) = 3k + j = (1j + 3k) N m. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Position vector r2 = (0i + 1j + 0k) m): tau = j x (2i + 3j - k) = 2(j x i) - 1(j x k) = -2k - i = (-1i - 2k) N m. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Position vector r3 = (0i + 0j + 1k) m): tau = k x (2i + 3j - k) = 2(k x i) + 3(k x j) = 2j - 3i = (-3i + 2j) N m. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Position vector r4 = (1i + 1j + 0k) m): tau = (i + j) x (2i + 3j - k) = (j + 3k) + (-i - 2k) = (-1i + 1j + 1k) N m. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A flywheel starts from rest and rotates with constant angular acceleration alpha = 4 rad/s^2. Match the kinematic rotational variables in List I with their values in List II:
List I:
A. Angular velocity after t = 3 seconds
B. Total angular displacement after t = 3 seconds
C. Average angular velocity over the first 3 seconds
D. Angular velocity after completing an angular displacement of 8 rad
List II:
I. 12 rad/s
II. 8 rad/s
III. 18 rad
IV. 6 rad/s
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Angular velocity after t = 3 seconds): omega = omega0 + alpha * t = 0 + 4 * 3 = 12 rad/s. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Total angular displacement after t = 3 seconds): theta = omega0 * t + 0.5 * alpha * t^2 = 0 + 0.5 * 4 * 9 = 18 rad. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Average angular velocity over the first 3 seconds): omega_avg = (omega0 + omega) / 2 = (0 + 12) / 2 = 6 rad/s. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Angular velocity after completing an angular displacement of 8 rad): omega^2 = omega0^2 + 2 * alpha * theta = 0 + 2 * 4 * 8 = 64 => omega = 8 rad/s. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match each symmetric body of mass M and radius R in List I with its radius of gyration k about its central axis in List II:
List I:
A. Thin circular ring of radius R
B. Uniform solid circular disc of radius R
C. Uniform solid sphere of radius R
D. Thin hollow spherical shell of radius R
List II:
I. R / sqrt(2)
II. sqrt(2/3) * R
III. R
IV. sqrt(2/5) * R
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Thin circular ring of radius R): I = M R^2 = M k^2 => k = R. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Uniform solid circular disc of radius R): I = (1/2) M R^2 = M k^2 => k = R / sqrt(2). Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Uniform solid sphere of radius R): I = (2/5) M R^2 = M k^2 => k = sqrt(2/5) * R. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Thin hollow spherical shell of radius R): I = (2/3) M R^2 = M k^2 => k = sqrt(2/3) * R. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A projectile of mass m is fired from the origin with initial speed u at angle theta to the horizontal. Match the quantities related to its angular momentum about the origin in List I with List II:
List I:
A. Magnitude of angular momentum at the highest point of trajectory
B. Magnitude of angular momentum just before landing on the ground
C. Torque due to gravity about the origin as a function of time t
D. Torque due to gravity about the origin at the highest point
List II:
I. (2m u^3 sin^2(theta) cos(theta)) / g
II. m g u t cos(theta)
III. (1/2) m u^2 sin(2*theta)
IV. (m u^3 sin^2(theta) cos(theta)) / (2g)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Magnitude of angular momentum at the highest point of trajectory): At peak: r = (R/2) i + H j, v = (u cos theta) i. L = m * (u cos theta) * H = m(u cos theta)(u^2 sin^2 theta / 2g). Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Magnitude of angular momentum just before landing on the ground): At landing: r = R i, v = (u cos theta) i - (u sin theta) j. L = m * R * (u sin theta) = 2m u^3 sin^2(theta) cos(theta) / g. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Torque due to gravity about the origin as a function of time t): tau = r x (m g) = (u cos theta * t) i x (-m g j) = -m g u t cos theta k. Magnitude is m g u t cos theta. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Torque due to gravity about the origin at the highest point): At highest point x = R/2 = u^2 sin(2 theta) / (2g). Torque tau = m g * (R/2) = (1/2) m u^2 sin(2 theta). Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the scenarios involving conservation of angular momentum in List I with the resulting physical state in List II:
List I:
A. A figure skater spinning at omega1 with moment of inertia I1 pulls arms in reducing inertia to I1/2
B. The rotational kinetic energy of the figure skater after pulling arms inward
C. A rotating disc of inertia I1 and angular speed omega1 dropped onto a coaxial stationary disc of inertia I2
D. A man of mass m standing on the rim of a disc (mass M, radius R) spinning at omega0 walks to the center
List II:
I. Common angular speed becomes I1*omega1 / (I1 + I2)
II. Final angular velocity doubles to 2 * omega1
III. Angular velocity increases by factor (M + 2m) / M
IV. Kinetic energy doubles to 2 * K1
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (A figure skater spinning at omega1 with moment of inertia I1 pulls arms in reducing inertia to I1/2): I1 * omega1 = (I1/2) * omega_f => omega_f = 2 * omega1. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (The rotational kinetic energy of the figure skater after pulling arms inward): K_f = (1/2)(I1/2)(2 omega1)^2 = I1 omega1^2 = 2 * ((1/2) I1 omega1^2) = 2 K1. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (A rotating disc of inertia I1 and angular speed omega1 dropped onto a coaxial stationary disc of inertia I2): Total angular momentum conservation: I1 omega1 = (I1 + I2) omega_common => omega_common = I1 omega1 / (I1 + I2). Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (A man of mass m standing on the rim of a disc (mass M, radius R) spinning at omega0 walks to the center): Initial I = (1/2)MR^2 + mR^2 = (M/2 + m)R^2. Final I = (1/2)MR^2. Ratio omega_f / omega0 = (M + 2m) / M. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Blocks m1 = 3 kg and m2 = 1 kg hang from a light cord passing over a pulley of mass M = 2 kg and radius R (I = 1/2 M R^2). Cord does not slip. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Linear acceleration a of the hanging blocks
B. Tension T1 in the cord segment supporting mass m1 = 3 kg
C. Tension T2 in the cord segment supporting mass m2 = 1 kg
D. Net torque acting on the pulley about its axle
List II:
I. 0.4 g
II. 0.4 g R (in N m)
III. 1.8 g (in Newtons)
IV. 1.4 g (in Newtons)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Linear acceleration a of the hanging blocks): Effective inertia I_eff = m1 + m2 + M/2 = 3 + 1 + 1 = 5 kg. Net driving force = (m1 - m2)g = 2g. a = 2g / 5 = 0.4 g. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Tension T1 in the cord segment supporting mass m1 = 3 kg): For descending block: m1 g - T1 = m1 a => T1 = 3(g - 0.4g) = 1.8 g N. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Tension T2 in the cord segment supporting mass m2 = 1 kg): For ascending block: T2 - m2 g = m2 a => T2 = 1(g + 0.4g) = 1.4 g N. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Net torque acting on the pulley about its axle): Net torque = (T1 - T2) R = (1.8g - 1.4g) R = 0.4 g R N m. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Uniform bodies roll down an inclined plane of inclination angle theta without slipping. Match each body in List I with its linear acceleration a_cm in List II:
List I:
A. Uniform solid sphere (k^2/R^2 = 2/5)
B. Uniform solid cylinder / disc (k^2/R^2 = 1/2)
C. Thin spherical shell (k^2/R^2 = 2/3)
D. Thin circular ring / hollow cylinder (k^2/R^2 = 1)
List II:
I. (2/3) g sin(theta)
II. (1/2) g sin(theta)
III. (5/7) g sin(theta)
IV. (3/5) g sin(theta)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Uniform solid sphere (k^2/R^2 = 2/5)): a = g sin theta / (1 + k^2/R^2) = g sin theta / (1 + 2/5) = (5/7) g sin theta. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Uniform solid cylinder / disc (k^2/R^2 = 1/2)): a = g sin theta / (1 + 1/2) = (2/3) g sin theta. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Thin spherical shell (k^2/R^2 = 2/3)): a = g sin theta / (1 + 2/3) = (3/5) g sin theta. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Thin circular ring / hollow cylinder (k^2/R^2 = 1)): a = g sin theta / (1 + 1) = (1/2) g sin theta. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the rolling bodies of mass M and radius R in List I with the minimum coefficient of static friction mu_min required to prevent slipping on an incline of angle theta in List II:
List I:
A. Thin circular ring (k^2/R^2 = 1)
B. Uniform solid disc (k^2/R^2 = 1/2)
C. Thin spherical shell (k^2/R^2 = 2/3)
D. Uniform solid sphere (k^2/R^2 = 2/5)
List II:
I. (1/3) tan(theta)
II. (2/5) tan(theta)
III. (2/7) tan(theta)
IV. (1/2) tan(theta)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Thin circular ring (k^2/R^2 = 1)): mu_min = tan theta / (1 + R^2/k^2) = tan theta / (1 + 1) = (1/2) tan theta. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Uniform solid disc (k^2/R^2 = 1/2)): mu_min = tan theta / (1 + 2) = (1/3) tan theta. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Thin spherical shell (k^2/R^2 = 2/3)): mu_min = tan theta / (1 + 3/2) = tan theta / (5/2) = (2/5) tan theta. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Uniform solid sphere (k^2/R^2 = 2/5)): mu_min = tan theta / (1 + 5/2) = tan theta / (7/2) = (2/7) tan theta. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A uniform thin rod of mass M and length L is pivoted horizontally at one end and released from rest. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Initial angular acceleration alpha at the moment of release
B. Initial linear acceleration of the free tip of the rod
C. Angular velocity omega when the rod swings through the vertical position
D. Vertical reaction force exerted by the hinge when rod passes through vertical
List II:
I. sqrt(3g / L)
II. 3g / (2L)
III. (5/2) Mg
IV. 1.5 g
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Initial angular acceleration alpha at the moment of release): Torque about pivot: Mg(L/2) = I alpha = (1/3 ML^2) alpha => alpha = 3g / (2L). Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Initial linear acceleration of the free tip of the rod): a_tip = L * alpha = L * (3g / (2L)) = 1.5 g. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Angular velocity omega when the rod swings through the vertical position): Energy conservation: Mg(L/2) = (1/2)(1/3 ML^2) omega^2 => omega = sqrt(3g / L). Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Vertical reaction force exerted by the hinge when rod passes through vertical): N - Mg = M a_cm = M omega^2 (L/2) = M(3g/L)(L/2) = 1.5 Mg => N = 2.5 Mg = (5/2) Mg. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A uniform solid cube of mass M and side edge 'a' rests on a rough horizontal floor (coefficient of static friction mu). A horizontal force F is applied at the top edge. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Critical horizontal force F_topple required to topple the cube
B. Maximum static friction available to prevent sliding
C. Condition on friction coefficient mu for the cube to topple before slipping
D. Condition on friction coefficient mu for the cube to slip before toppling
List II:
I. (1/2) Mg
II. mu < 0.5
III. mu * Mg
IV. mu > 0.5
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Critical horizontal force F_topple required to topple the cube): Torque balance about front tipping edge: F * a = Mg * (a/2) => F_topple = (1/2) Mg. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum static friction available to prevent sliding): Normal reaction on flat floor is N = Mg; max static friction is f_s,max = mu * N = mu * Mg. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Condition on friction coefficient mu for the cube to topple before slipping): Topple before slip requires F_topple < f_s,max => 0.5 Mg < mu Mg => mu > 0.5. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Condition on friction coefficient mu for the cube to slip before toppling): Slip before topple requires f_s,max < F_topple => mu Mg < 0.5 Mg => mu < 0.5. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R is given initial forward velocity v0 on a rough horizontal floor with zero initial spin (omega0 = 0). Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Time t_p taken to achieve pure rolling without slipping
B. Linear velocity v_p of the sphere when pure rolling is established
C. Angular velocity omega_p when pure rolling is established
D. Fraction of initial kinetic energy dissipated as heat during transition
List II:
I. (5/7) v0
II. 2/7 of initial kinetic energy
III. 2*v0 / (7*mu*g)
IV. 5*v0 / (7*R)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Time t_p taken to achieve pure rolling without slipping): Friction f = mu Mg backwards. dv/dt = -mu g, R domega/dt = 5 mu g / 2. Pure rolling: v = R omega => v0 - mu g t = 2.5 mu g t => t = 2v0 / (7 mu g). Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Linear velocity v_p of the sphere when pure rolling is established): v_p = v0 - mu g t_p = v0 - mu g (2v0 / (7 mu g)) = (5/7) v0. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Angular velocity omega_p when pure rolling is established): omega_p = v_p / R = (5/7) v0 / R = 5 v0 / (7 R). Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Fraction of initial kinetic energy dissipated as heat during transition): Initial K = 1/2 M v0^2. Final K = 1/2 M v_p^2 (1 + 2/5) = 7/10 M (25/49 v0^2) = 5/14 M v0^2. Loss = 1/2 - 5/14 = 2/14 = 1/7 of M v0^2 = 2/7 of K_initial. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match each physical planar motion in List I with the location of its Instantaneous Axis of Rotation (IAOR) in List II:
List I:
A. Uniform cylinder rolling without slipping on a fixed horizontal surface
B. Uniform ladder sliding down with ends in contact with perpendicular wall and floor
C. Uniform cylinder of radius R rolling without slipping on a cart moving with speed vc
D. A free body with center of mass velocity v_cm and angular velocity omega in plane motion
List II:
I. Intersection of perpendicular normals to the wall and floor at the ladder ends
II. Line of contact between cylinder and cart moving at velocity vc
III. Point displaced from CM by vector r = (omega x v_cm) / omega^2
IV. The instantaneous line of contact with the ground
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Uniform cylinder rolling without slipping on a fixed horizontal surface): For pure rolling on stationary floor, contact points have zero instantaneous velocity, defining the IAOR. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Uniform ladder sliding down with ends in contact with perpendicular wall and floor): Velocity of top end is along wall and bottom end along floor; IAOR lies at intersection of line normals to velocities. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Uniform cylinder of radius R rolling without slipping on a cart moving with speed vc): Points along the contact line move at velocity vc relative to ground and zero velocity relative to cart. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (A free body with center of mass velocity v_cm and angular velocity omega in plane motion): v_P = v_cm + omega x r = 0 implies r = (omega x v_cm) / omega^2 perpendicular to v_cm. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A uniform thin rod of mass M and length L is pivoted at one end on a frictionless vertical axis. A bullet of mass m (m << M) with speed v0 hits the rod perpendicularly at distance x from the pivot and embeds. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Moment of inertia of the combined system about the pivot axle
B. Angular velocity omega immediately after collision
C. Impact distance x from pivot (center of percussion) yielding zero hinge reaction impulse
D. Hinge reaction impulse when bullet strikes at the extreme tip x = L (with m << M)
List II:
I. (2/3) L
II. (1/3) M L^2 + m x^2
III. (1/2) m v0 in the forward direction
IV. m v0 x / ((1/3) M L^2 + m x^2)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Moment of inertia of the combined system about the pivot axle): I_total = I_rod + I_bullet = (1/3) M L^2 + m x^2. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Angular velocity omega immediately after collision): Conservation of angular momentum about pivot: m v0 x = I_total omega => omega = m v0 x / ((1/3) M L^2 + m x^2). Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Impact distance x from pivot (center of percussion) yielding zero hinge reaction impulse): Hinge impulse J = M v_cm - m v0 = M (omega L/2) - m v0 = 0. Substituting omega gives x = 2L/3. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Hinge reaction impulse when bullet strikes at the extreme tip x = L (with m << M)): With x = L: omega = 3 m v0 / (M L). Hinge impulse J = M(omega L/2) - m v0 = 1.5 m v0 - m v0 = 0.5 m v0 forward. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rests on a horizontal plank which accelerates horizontally at constant a0. The cylinder rolls without slipping on the plank. Match List I with List II:
List I:
A. Acceleration of the center of mass of the cylinder relative to ground
