Step 3: Match item C (Quarter-wave plate (QWP) thickness t = λ / (4 |n_o - n_e|)): Introduces a phase difference of Δφ = π / 2 (path difference λ / 4) between o- and e-components. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Full-wave plate thickness t = λ / |n_o - n_e|): Path difference λ produces no net change in polarization state for wavelength λ. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the coherence concepts and fringe visibility parameters in List I with their mathematical expressions or physical meanings in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum permissible source width s for observing clear fringes in YDSE
B. Temporal coherence length L_c of a quasi-monochromatic source of spectral width Δλ
C. Effect on fringes when path difference exceeds temporal coherence length (Δx > L_c)
D. Fringe visibility V in an interference pattern
List II:
I. s ≤ λ D_s / d
II. λ² / Δλ
III. Fringes wash out and disappear completely
IV. (I_max - I_min) / (I_max + I_min)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum permissible source width s for observing clear fringes in YDSE): Spatial coherence requires source angular size s/D_s to be smaller than fringe angular spacing λ/d. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Temporal coherence length L_c of a quasi-monochromatic source of spectral width Δλ): Length over which phase correlation persists: L_c = c τ_c ≈ c / Δν = λ² / Δλ. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Effect on fringes when path difference exceeds temporal coherence length (Δx > L_c)): Wave packets no longer overlap in time, destroying phase correlation between interfering beams. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Fringe visibility V in an interference pattern): Standard Michelson definition of fringe contrast; V = 1 for pure interference, V = 0 for no fringes. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A solution of an optically active substance (e.g. sugar in water) rotates the plane of polarization of linearly polarized light. Match the polarimetry parameters in List I with their definitions or formulas in List II:
List I:
A. Laurent half-shade device in a polarimeter
B. Angle of optical rotation θ
C. Dextrorotatory vs Levorotatory substances
D. Specific rotation [α] at temperature T and wavelength D
List II:
I. Divides field of view into two halves with different polarization angles for high-precision extinction matching
II. [α] × l × c
III. Rotates plane of polarization clockwise (right) vs counterclockwise (left) facing oncoming beam
IV. θ / (l × c)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Laurent half-shade device in a polarimeter): Enables high-precision matching of two halves of unequal brightness to find optical extinction. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Angle of optical rotation θ): Biot's law: rotation is proportional to specific rotation [α], path length l (dm), and concentration c (g/cm³). Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Dextrorotatory vs Levorotatory substances): Dextrorotatory rotates rightwards (+) while levorotatory rotates leftwards (-). Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Specific rotation [α] at temperature T and wavelength D): Optical rotation produced by 1 decimeter of solution containing 1 g/cm³ of active substance. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A convex lens of focal length f is cut along its principal axis into two halves, which are separated by a small gap s. A monochromatic point source is placed on the axis at distance u = 2f in front of the lens. Match the Billet split lens parameters in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Distance v of the two real images (coherent sources S1, S2) from the lens
B. Nature of the coherent sources S1 and S2
C. Separation d between the two coherent source images S1 and S2
D. Fringe width β on a screen placed at distance D from the split lens (D > 2f)
List II:
I. 2f
II. Real coherent images formed by refraction through the two lens halves
III. 2s
IV. λ (D - 2f) / (2s)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Distance v of the two real images (coherent sources S1, S2) from the lens): Using thin lens formula 1/v - 1/(-2f) = 1/f gives 1/v = 1/f - 1/(2f) = 1/(2f), so v = 2f. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Nature of the coherent sources S1 and S2): The two halves form two distinct real point images in space that act as coherent sources. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Separation d between the two coherent source images S1 and S2): Each half-lens is displaced by s/2 from the source, so images are separated by d = s(1 + v/u) = s(1 + 1) = 2s. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Fringe width β on a screen placed at distance D from the split lens (D > 2f)): Distance from coherent source plane to screen is D' = D - 2f; slit separation is d = 2s, giving β = λ D' / d. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the fundamental parameters of the photoelectric effect in List I with their defining physical descriptions in List II:
List I:
A. Work function (phi_0)
B. Threshold frequency (nu_0)
C. Stopping potential (V_0)
D. Saturation photocurrent (I_sat)
List II:
I. Maximum current obtained when all photoelectrons emitted per second reach the anode
II. Minimum energy required to liberate an electron from the metal surface with zero velocity
III. Minimum frequency of incident radiation below which no photoelectric emission takes place
IV. Negative collector potential that reduces the photocurrent to zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Work function (phi_0)): The work function represents the binding energy of the most loosely bound conduction electrons to the metal lattice.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Threshold frequency (nu_0)): Photoemission requires photon energy h*nu >= phi_0, so nu_0 = phi_0 / h.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Stopping potential (V_0)): At stopping potential, maximum kinetic energy of electrons equals the electrostatic work done: K_max = e * V_0.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Saturation photocurrent (I_sat)): Saturation current is directly proportional to the intensity of incident light for a given frequency.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the de Broglie wavelength expressions for particles with kinetic energy K or accelerating potential V in List I with their formula in List II:
List I:
A. Electron accelerated from rest through potential difference V
B. Proton accelerated from rest through potential difference V
C. Alpha particle accelerated through potential difference V
D. Thermal neutron in equilibrium at absolute temperature T
List II:
I. lambda = 0.101 / sqrt(V) A = h / sqrt(8 m_p e V)
II. lambda = h / sqrt(3 m_n k_B T)
III. lambda = 12.27 / sqrt(V) A = h / sqrt(2 m_e e V)
IV. lambda = 0.286 / sqrt(V) A = h / sqrt(2 m_p e V)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Electron accelerated from rest through potential difference V): For an electron, substituting h, m_e, e yields lambda = 1.227 / sqrt(V) nm = 12.27 / sqrt(V) A.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Proton accelerated from rest through potential difference V): With proton mass m_p approx 1836 m_e, lambda_p = 0.286 / sqrt(V) A.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Alpha particle accelerated through potential difference V): With m_alpha = 4 m_p and q_alpha = 2 e, sqrt(2 m q) = sqrt(16 m_p e) = 4 sqrt(m_p e), giving lambda_alpha = 0.101 / sqrt(V) A.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Thermal neutron in equilibrium at absolute temperature T): Average translational kinetic energy of thermal neutron is K = (3/2) k_B T, so p = sqrt(2 m_n (3/2 k_B T)) = sqrt(3 m_n k_B T).. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the observed photoelectric phenomena in List I with their physical significance in List II:
List I:
A. Instantaneous emission (< 10^-9 s)
B. Existence of threshold frequency
C. Linear variation of V_0 with frequency
D. Photocurrent proportional to intensity
List II:
I. Demonstrates that radiation transfers energy in discrete packets (E = h*nu)
II. Confirms Einstein's energy conservation equation e*V_0 = h*nu - phi_0
III. Reflects that number of emitted electrons is proportional to the incident photon arrival rate
IV. Disproves classical wave theory where energy is absorbed continuously over the wavefront
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Instantaneous emission (< 10^-9 s)): In classical theory, wavefront distributes energy continuously requiring hours, while in photon theory, absorption is a localized single collision.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Existence of threshold frequency): If photon energy is less than phi_0, no electron can be liberated regardless of the wave intensity.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Linear variation of V_0 with frequency): The slope of V_0 vs nu is h/e, which is an invariant universal constant.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Photocurrent proportional to intensity): Intensity I = n*h*nu where n is photon flux; doubling intensity doubles the number of photons striking the plate per second.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the properties of a photon of frequency nu and wavelength lambda in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Energy of a single photon
B. Linear momentum of photon
C. Rest mass of photon
D. Dynamic (effective) mass of photon
List II:
I. E = h*nu = hc / lambda
II. m = h*nu / c^2 = h / (c * lambda)
III. p = h / lambda = h*nu / c
IV. Strictly zero
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Energy of a single photon): Energy of a quantum of light is proportional to frequency according to Planck.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Linear momentum of photon): According to de Broglie and relativistic energy-momentum relation E = pc for a massless particle.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Rest mass of photon): Photons always travel at speed of light c in vacuum and have zero invariant rest mass.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Dynamic (effective) mass of photon): From Einstein's mass-energy equivalence E = m c^2 = h*nu.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Monochromatic light of wavelength lambda = 248 nm (photon energy hc/lambda = 5.0 eV) is incident on four different metals. Match each metal in List I with its maximum kinetic energy (K_max) and stopping potential (V_0) in List II:
List I:
A. Metal A with work function phi_0 = 1.8 eV
B. Metal B with work function phi_0 = 2.5 eV
C. Metal C with work function phi_0 = 3.7 eV
D. Metal D with work function phi_0 = 4.4 eV
List II:
I. K_max = 1.3 eV, V_0 = 1.3 V
II. K_max = 3.2 eV, V_0 = 3.2 V
III. K_max = 0.6 eV, V_0 = 0.6 V
IV. K_max = 2.5 eV, V_0 = 2.5 V
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Metal A with work function phi_0 = 1.8 eV): From Einstein's equation, K_max = E - phi_0 = 5.0 - 1.8 = 3.2 eV, hence V_0 = 3.2 V.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Metal B with work function phi_0 = 2.5 eV): K_max = 5.0 - 2.5 = 2.5 eV, so V_0 = 2.5 V.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Metal C with work function phi_0 = 3.7 eV): K_max = 5.0 - 3.7 = 1.3 eV, so V_0 = 1.3 V.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Metal D with work function phi_0 = 4.4 eV): K_max = 5.0 - 4.4 = 0.6 eV, so V_0 = 0.6 V.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the graphical characteristics of the photoelectric effect in List I with their physical representations in List II:
List I:
A. Slope of stopping potential V_0 versus frequency nu
B. Intercept on the frequency axis of the V_0 vs nu graph
C. Negative intercept on the potential axis of the V_0 vs nu graph
D. Slope of maximum kinetic energy K_max versus frequency nu
List II:
I. Threshold frequency nu_0 of the specific metal
II. Planck's constant h
III. h/e, a universal constant identical for all photosensitive metals
IV. -phi_0/e, directly proportional to the work function
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Slope of stopping potential V_0 versus frequency nu): Since V_0 = (h/e)*nu - phi_0/e, the slope is dV_0/dnu = h/e.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Intercept on the frequency axis of the V_0 vs nu graph): At V_0 = 0, nu = phi_0/h = nu_0.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Negative intercept on the potential axis of the V_0 vs nu graph): Extrapolating to nu = 0 gives V = -phi_0/e.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Slope of maximum kinetic energy K_max versus frequency nu): Since K_max = h*nu - phi_0, the slope is dK_max/dnu = h.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the pairs of particles and specified conditions in List I with the corresponding ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths in List II:
List I:
A. Ratio lambda_p / lambda_alpha for proton and alpha particle with equal kinetic energy
B. Ratio lambda_e / lambda_p for electron and proton with equal linear momentum
C. Ratio lambda_p / lambda_alpha for proton and alpha particle accelerated from rest through the same potential V
D. Ratio lambda_1 / lambda_2 for a particle whose kinetic energy is increased to 9 times its initial value
List II:
I. Ratio is 3
II. Ratio is 2*sqrt(2) approx 2.83
III. Ratio is 1
IV. Ratio is 2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Ratio lambda_p / lambda_alpha for proton and alpha particle with equal kinetic energy): lambda = h / sqrt(2 m K). With m_alpha = 4 m_p and K_p = K_alpha, lambda_p / lambda_alpha = sqrt(m_alpha / m_p) = sqrt(4) = 2.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Ratio lambda_e / lambda_p for electron and proton with equal linear momentum): lambda = h/p. Since p_e = p_p, lambda_e / lambda_p = 1.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Ratio lambda_p / lambda_alpha for proton and alpha particle accelerated from rest through the same potential V): lambda = h / sqrt(2 m q V). lambda_p / lambda_alpha = sqrt((m_alpha q_alpha)/(m_p q_p)) = sqrt(4 * 2) = sqrt(8) = 2*sqrt(2).. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Ratio lambda_1 / lambda_2 for a particle whose kinetic energy is increased to 9 times its initial value): K_2 = 9 K_1 implies p_2 = 3 p_1 implies lambda_1 / lambda_2 = p_2 / p_1 = 3.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A parallel beam of light of power P = 60 W falls on different surfaces in vacuum. Match the surface conditions in List I with the magnitude of the radiation force exerted on the surface in List II (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s):
List I:
A. Perfectly absorbing surface at normal incidence
B. Perfectly reflecting surface at normal incidence
C. Surface with reflection coefficient r = 0.5 at normal incidence
D. Perfectly reflecting surface at angle of incidence theta = 60 degrees
List II:
I. 4.0 x 10^-7 N
II. 2.0 x 10^-7 N
III. 1.0 x 10^-7 N
IV. 3.0 x 10^-7 N
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Perfectly absorbing surface at normal incidence): Force F = P/c = 60 / (3 x 10^8) = 2.0 x 10^-7 N.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Perfectly reflecting surface at normal incidence): Force F = 2P/c = 2 * 60 / (3 x 10^8) = 4.0 x 10^-7 N.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Surface with reflection coefficient r = 0.5 at normal incidence): Force F = (1+r) P / c = 1.5 * 60 / (3 x 10^8) = 3.0 x 10^-7 N.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Perfectly reflecting surface at angle of incidence theta = 60 degrees): Force normal to surface is F = 2 P cos^2(60)/c = 2 P (1/4)/c = P / (2c) = 1.0 x 10^-7 N.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the aspects of the Davisson-Germer electron diffraction experiment in List I with their descriptions and values in List II:
List I:
A. Accelerating potential giving the most pronounced diffraction peak
B. Scattering angle phi between incident and scattered beam at peak
C. Glancing angle theta with the Bragg crystal planes
D. de Broglie wavelength computed from accelerating potential
List II:
I. lambda = 12.27 / sqrt(54) A approx 1.67 A
II. 50 degrees
III. 54 V
IV. theta = 90 - phi/2 = 65 degrees
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Accelerating potential giving the most pronounced diffraction peak): A distinct peak in the scattered electron intensity occurs at an accelerating voltage of 54 V.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Scattering angle phi between incident and scattered beam at peak): The detector records a sharp maximum at a scattering angle of phi = 50 degrees.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Glancing angle theta with the Bragg crystal planes): The Bragg glancing angle is theta = 90 - 50/2 = 65 degrees.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (de Broglie wavelength computed from accelerating potential): The de Broglie formula gives lambda = 1.67 A, matching Bragg's formula 2d sin(theta) = 2(0.91 A) sin(65) = 1.65 A.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match each light source of given power and wavelength in List I with the number of photons emitted per second in List II (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, c = 3 x 10^8 m/s):
List I:
A. Laser with power P = 3.315 mW and wavelength lambda = 600 nm
B. Laser with power P = 6.63 mW and wavelength lambda = 500 nm
C. Laser with power P = 9.945 mW and wavelength lambda = 400 nm
D. Laser with power P = 19.89 mW and wavelength lambda = 300 nm
List II:
I. 1.0 x 10^16 photons/s
II. 2.0 x 10^16 photons/s
III. 3.0 x 10^16 photons/s
IV. 1.67 x 10^16 photons/s
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Laser with power P = 3.315 mW and wavelength lambda = 600 nm): Energy per photon E = hc/lambda = (6.63e-34 * 3e8)/(600e-9) = 3.315e-19 J. Number of photons n = P/E = 3.315e-3 / 3.315e-19 = 1.0e16 s^-1.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Laser with power P = 6.63 mW and wavelength lambda = 500 nm): Energy per photon E = (6.63e-34 * 3e8)/(500e-9) = 3.978e-19 J. Rate n = 6.63e-3 / 3.978e-19 approx 1.67e16 s^-1.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Laser with power P = 9.945 mW and wavelength lambda = 400 nm): Energy per photon E = (6.63e-34 * 3e8)/(400e-9) = 4.9725e-19 J. Rate n = 9.945e-3 / 4.9725e-19 = 2.0e16 s^-1.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Laser with power P = 19.89 mW and wavelength lambda = 300 nm): Energy per photon E = (6.63e-34 * 3e8)/(300e-9) = 6.63e-19 J. Rate n = 19.89e-3 / 6.63e-19 = 3.0e16 s^-1.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the parameter variations in a photoelectric experiment in List I with their direct physical consequences in List II:
List I:
A. Frequency of incident radiation is doubled while keeping intensity constant
B. Intensity of incident radiation is doubled while keeping frequency constant
C. Distance d of a small point light source from the cathode is doubled
D. Cathode material is replaced with one having higher work function phi_0
List II:
I. Saturation current drops to one-fourth, while stopping potential remains unchanged
II. Saturation current doubles, while stopping potential remains strictly unchanged
III. Threshold frequency increases and stopping potential decreases for the same incident light
IV. Stopping potential increases by more than a factor of 2, while saturation current decreases
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Frequency of incident radiation is doubled while keeping intensity constant): With constant intensity I = n*h*nu, doubling nu halves photon flux n, decreasing saturation current; e*V_2 = 2*h*nu - phi = 2*(e*V_1 + phi) - phi = 2*e*V_1 + phi > 2*e*V_1.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Intensity of incident radiation is doubled while keeping frequency constant): Saturation current is proportional to photon flux, which doubles with intensity, but V_0 depends only on nu.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Distance d of a small point light source from the cathode is doubled): By the inverse-square law, intensity on cathode becomes I/4, so saturation current is I_sat/4; frequency and hence V_0 are unaffected.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Cathode material is replaced with one having higher work function phi_0): Higher work function means higher nu_0 = phi_0/h and smaller maximum kinetic energy K_max = h*nu - phi_0.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the particle relativistic conditions in List I with the relation for its de Broglie wavelength lambda in terms of rest mass m_0 and kinetic energy K in List II:
List I:
A. Non-relativistic limit (K << m_0 c^2)
B. Particle with kinetic energy K = m_0 c^2
C. Particle with kinetic energy K = 3 m_0 c^2
D. Ultra-relativistic limit (K >> m_0 c^2)
List II:
I. lambda approx h*c / K
II. lambda = h / sqrt(2 m_0 K)
III. lambda = h / (sqrt(15) m_0 c)
IV. lambda = h / (sqrt(3) m_0 c)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Non-relativistic limit (K << m_0 c^2)): In classical limit, p = sqrt(2 m_0 K), so lambda = h / sqrt(2 m_0 K).. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Particle with kinetic energy K = m_0 c^2): Total energy E = K + m_0 c^2 = 2 m_0 c^2. Momentum p = (1/c) sqrt(E^2 - m_0^2 c^4) = sqrt(3) m_0 c, giving lambda = h / (sqrt(3) m_0 c).. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Particle with kinetic energy K = 3 m_0 c^2): Total energy E = 4 m_0 c^2. Momentum p = (1/c) sqrt(16 m_0^2 c^4 - m_0^2 c^4) = sqrt(15) m_0 c, so lambda = h / (sqrt(15) m_0 c).. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Ultra-relativistic limit (K >> m_0 c^2)): When K >> m_0 c^2, total energy E approx K approx p*c, hence p approx K/c and lambda approx hc/K.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Photoelectrons emitted with maximum kinetic energy K_max from a planar cathode enter a uniform transverse magnetic field B parallel to the plate. Match the parameters in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Radius of the circular trajectory of the fastest photoelectrons
B. Minimum magnetic field required to prevent photoelectrons from reaching a parallel anode at distance d
C. Time taken by the fastest electrons to return to the cathode
D. Maximum magnetic Lorentz force acting on any emitted photoelectron
List II:
I. F_max = B * sqrt(2 e^2 K_max / m_e)
II. T_half = pi * m_e / (e * B)
III. R_max = sqrt(2 m_e K_max) / (e * B)
IV. B_min = sqrt(2 m_e K_max) / (e * d)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Radius of the circular trajectory of the fastest photoelectrons): Centripetal force e * v_max * B = m_e * v_max^2 / R, so R_max = m_e * v_max / (e * B) = sqrt(2 m_e K_max) / (e * B).. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Minimum magnetic field required to prevent photoelectrons from reaching a parallel anode at distance d): To just miss the plate, the radius of the grazing orbit satisfies R_max <= d, giving B >= sqrt(2 m_e K_max) / (e * d).. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Time taken by the fastest electrons to return to the cathode): The electron executes a half-circle before striking back the cathode, taking time t = T/2 = pi * m_e / (e * B), independent of velocity.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Maximum magnetic Lorentz force acting on any emitted photoelectron): F_max = e * v_max * B = e * sqrt(2 K_max / m_e) * B = B * sqrt(2 e^2 K_max / m_e).. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
An isolated metal sphere of radius R and work function phi_0 is placed in vacuum and irradiated by monochromatic light of wavelength lambda (hc/lambda > phi_0). Match the electro-optical quantities in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum electric potential attained by the sphere
B. Total positive charge accumulated on the sphere at cutoff
C. Total number of electrons ejected before photoemission ceases
D. Effect of doubling the radius of the sphere
List II:
I. N = [4*pi*epsilon_0*R / e^2] * (hc/lambda - phi_0)
II. Potential V_max remains unchanged, while total accumulated charge doubles
III. Q_max = [4*pi*epsilon_0*R / e] * (hc/lambda - phi_0)
IV. V_max = (1/e) * (hc/lambda - phi_0)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum electric potential attained by the sphere): Photoemission stops when the retarding electrostatic surface potential equals the stopping potential V_0.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Total positive charge accumulated on the sphere at cutoff): For an isolated conducting sphere, V_max = Q_max / (4 pi epsilon_0 R), hence Q_max = 4 pi epsilon_0 R V_max.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Total number of electrons ejected before photoemission ceases): Total number of lost electrons is N = Q_max / e.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Effect of doubling the radius of the sphere): V_max depends solely on frequency and work function, whereas Q_max is proportional to R.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
In Compton scattering, a photon of initial wavelength lambda_0 collides with a stationary free electron of rest mass m_e. Match each scattering angle theta or condition in List I with its resulting wavelength shift Delta lambda or kinetic energy in List II (where lambda_C = h / (m_e c) approx 0.0243 A):
List I:
A. Scattering angle theta = 90 degrees
B. Scattering angle theta = 180 degrees (backscattering)
C. Scattering angle theta = 60 degrees
D. Kinetic energy acquired by recoil electron for theta = 180 degrees
List II:
I. Delta lambda = 2*lambda_C approx 0.0485 A
II. Delta lambda = lambda_C approx 0.0243 A
III. Delta lambda = 0.5*lambda_C approx 0.0121 A
IV. K_e = 2*h*c*lambda_C / [lambda_0 * (lambda_0 + 2*lambda_C)]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Scattering angle theta = 90 degrees): The Compton formula gives Delta lambda = lambda_C (1 - cos 90) = lambda_C.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Scattering angle theta = 180 degrees (backscattering)): For theta = 180 degrees, Delta lambda = lambda_C (1 - (-1)) = 2 lambda_C, which is the maximum possible wavelength shift.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Scattering angle theta = 60 degrees): For theta = 60 degrees, Delta lambda = lambda_C (1 - cos 60) = lambda_C (1 - 0.5) = 0.5 lambda_C.. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Kinetic energy acquired by recoil electron for theta = 180 degrees): By energy conservation, K_e = hc/lambda_0 - hc/(lambda_0 + 2 lambda_C) = 2 h c lambda_C / [lambda_0 (lambda_0 + 2 lambda_C)].. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the matter wave velocity concepts for a relativistic particle with energy E = hbar*omega = sqrt(p^2 c^2 + m_0^2 c^4) in List I with their expressions and properties in List II:
List I:
A. Phase velocity of matter wave (v_p = omega / k)
B. Group velocity of matter wave (v_g = domega / dk)
C. Product of phase velocity and group velocity
D. Ratio v_g / v_p for a non-relativistic particle (E_k = p^2 / 2m)
List II:
I. v_p = c^2 / v > c
II. v_g = dE/dp = v
III. v_g / v_p = 2
IV. v_p * v_g = c^2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Phase velocity of matter wave (v_p = omega / k)): Since omega = E/hbar and k = p/hbar, v_p = E/p = gamma m_0 c^2 / (gamma m_0 v) = c^2 / v, which exceeds the speed of light in vacuum.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Group velocity of matter wave (v_g = domega / dk)): Differentiating E^2 = p^2 c^2 + m_0^2 c^4 gives 2E dE = 2p c^2 dp, so dE/dp = c^2 p / E = c^2 (gamma m_0 v) / (gamma m_0 c^2) = v.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Product of phase velocity and group velocity): v_p * v_g = (c^2 / v) * v = c^2.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Ratio v_g / v_p for a non-relativistic particle (E_k = p^2 / 2m)): In non-relativistic mechanics, v_p = E/p = (p^2 / 2m)/p = v/2, while v_g = dE/dp = p/m = v, hence v_g / v_p = 2.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A parallel beam of monochromatic light of intensity I, cross-sectional area A, and wavelength lambda is incident on a flat metal plate at angle of incidence theta. Match the physical quantities in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Number of photons striking the plate per second
B. Power incident per unit area of the plate surface
C. Saturation photocurrent for quantum efficiency eta
D. Radiation force exerted on a perfectly absorbing plate
List II:
I. I_surface = I * cos(theta)
II. F = I * A / c in the direction of the incident beam
III. N_ph = I * A * lambda / (h * c)
IV. i_sat = eta * e * I * A * lambda / (h * c)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Number of photons striking the plate per second): Total power in the beam is P = I A. Since the entire beam is intercepted, photon arrival rate is P/E = (I A)/(hc/lambda) = I A lambda / (hc).. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Power incident per unit area of the plate surface): The intercepted cross-sectional area spreads over surface area A / cos(theta), so surface intensity is I cos(theta).. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Saturation photocurrent for quantum efficiency eta): Photocurrent is i_sat = eta * e * N_ph = eta e I A lambda / (hc).. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Radiation force exerted on a perfectly absorbing plate): Total beam momentum delivered per second is P/c = (I A)/c along the beam propagation vector.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
In an electron microscope, electrons are accelerated by potential difference V. Match the microscope operational quantities in List I with their functional dependencies or values in List II:
List I:
A. de Broglie wavelength for accelerating voltage V = 50 kV (non-relativistic approximation)
B. Functional dependence of limit of resolution d_min on accelerating potential V
C. Factor by which resolving power increases when V is quadrupled from 25 kV to 100 kV
D. Ratio of resolving power using 50 kV electrons to an optical microscope using lambda = 5500 A
List II:
I. Factor of 2
II. lambda approx 0.055 A = 5.5 pm
III. Approx 10^5 times greater
IV. d_min proportional to V^(-1/2)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (de Broglie wavelength for accelerating voltage V = 50 kV (non-relativistic approximation)): lambda = 12.27 / sqrt(50000) A approx 12.27 / 223.6 approx 0.0549 A.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Functional dependence of limit of resolution d_min on accelerating potential V): By Abbe's criterion, d_min proportional to lambda proportional to 1/sqrt(V).. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Factor by which resolving power increases when V is quadrupled from 25 kV to 100 kV): Resolving power is 1/d_min proportional to sqrt(V). Quadrupling V doubles resolving power.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Ratio of resolving power using 50 kV electrons to an optical microscope using lambda = 5500 A): Ratio is lambda_light / lambda_electron approx 5500 / 0.055 = 10^5.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A photocell is connected in series with a capacitor C and an illuminated metal surface of work function phi_0. When light of frequency nu > phi_0/h shines on it, match the steady-state electrical parameters in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Maximum potential difference across the capacitor
B. Maximum charge stored on the capacitor
C. Electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor at equilibrium
D. Ratio of stored energy if frequency is increased such that stopping potential is tripled
List II:
I. Increases by a factor of 9
II. Q_max = C * (h*nu - phi_0) / e
III. U_E = C * (h*nu - phi_0)^2 / (2 * e^2)
IV. V_C = (h*nu - phi_0) / e
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum potential difference across the capacitor): Electrons continue charging the capacitor until the potential barrier halts even the fastest photoelectrons, i.e., V_C = V_0 = (h*nu - phi_0)/e.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum charge stored on the capacitor): From Q = C * V_C.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor at equilibrium): Energy stored is U = (1/2) C V_C^2 = C(h*nu - phi_0)^2 / (2 e^2).. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Ratio of stored energy if frequency is increased such that stopping potential is tripled): Since U is proportional to V_0^2, tripling the stopping potential increases the stored energy by 3^2 = 9.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A metal plate with work function phi_0 = 2.0 eV is simultaneously illuminated by two monochromatic light sources of wavelengths lambda_1 = 310 nm (E_1 = 4.0 eV) and lambda_2 = 620 nm (E_2 = 2.0 eV). Match the experimental observations in List I with their quantitative values in List II:
List I:
A. Overall stopping potential V_0 required to completely reduce photocurrent to zero
B. Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons expressed in Joules (1 eV = 1.6 x 10^-19 J)
C. Maximum speed of emitted photoelectrons (m_e = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)
D. Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted by source lambda_2
List II:
I. 2.0 V
II. v_max approx 8.4 x 10^5 m/s
III. 3.2 x 10^-19 J
IV. 0 eV (at threshold, emission with zero kinetic energy)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Overall stopping potential V_0 required to completely reduce photocurrent to zero): The stopping potential is determined by the most energetic photoelectrons produced by lambda_1: e * V_0 = E_1 - phi_0 = 4.0 - 2.0 = 2.0 eV, so V_0 = 2.0 V.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons expressed in Joules (1 eV = 1.6 x 10^-19 J)): K_max = 2.0 eV = 2.0 * 1.6e-19 = 3.2e-19 J.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Maximum speed of emitted photoelectrons (m_e = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)): v_max = sqrt(2 K_max / m_e) = sqrt(2 * 3.2e-19 / 9.1e-31) approx 8.38 x 10^5 m/s.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted by source lambda_2): For lambda_2, photon energy E_2 = 2.0 eV = phi_0, so photoelectrons are ejected with zero kinetic energy.. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the physical quantities of an electron in the n-th Bohr orbit of a hydrogen-like atom of atomic number Z in List I with their proportionality in List II:
List I:
A. Orbital radius r_n
B. Orbital velocity v_n
C. Total orbital energy E_n
D. Orbital angular momentum L_n
List II:
I. Proportional to n (independent of Z)
II. Proportional to n^2 / Z
III. Proportional to Z / n
IV. Proportional to -Z^2 / n^2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Orbital radius r_n): r_n = epsilon_0 n^2 h^2 / (pi m Z e^2) proportional to n^2 / Z.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Orbital velocity v_n): v_n = Z e^2 / (2 epsilon_0 n h) proportional to Z / n.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Total orbital energy E_n): E_n = -m Z^2 e^4 / (8 epsilon_0^2 n^2 h^2) proportional to -Z^2 / n^2.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Orbital angular momentum L_n): Bohr's quantization postulate is L_n = n * h / (2 pi).. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the hydrogen spectral emission series in List I with the electromagnetic spectrum region in which they occur in List II:
List I:
A. Lyman series (n_1 = 1, n_2 = 2, 3, ...)
B. Balmer series (n_1 = 2, n_2 = 3, 4, ...)
C. Paschen series (n_1 = 3, n_2 = 4, 5, ...)
D. Pfund series (n_1 = 5, n_2 = 6, 7, ...)
List II:
I. Near-infrared (Near-IR) region
II. Far-infrared (Far-IR) region
III. Ultraviolet (UV) region
IV. Visible and near-ultraviolet region
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Lyman series (n_1 = 1, n_2 = 2, 3, ...)): Transitions to the ground state n=1 have energy >= 10.2 eV, corresponding to lambda <= 1216 A in the UV region.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Balmer series (n_1 = 2, n_2 = 3, 4, ...)): Transitions to n=2 have wavelengths from 6563 A to 3646 A, lying largely in the visible spectrum.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Paschen series (n_1 = 3, n_2 = 4, 5, ...)): Transitions to n=3 have wavelengths starting from 1875 nm in the near infrared.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Pfund series (n_1 = 5, n_2 = 6, 7, ...)): Transitions to n=5 have long wavelengths falling in the far infrared.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the nuclear terminology and properties in List I with their defining characteristics in List II:
List I:
A. Nuclear radius R
B. Nuclear matter density rho
C. Isotopes
D. Isobars
List II:
I. Roughly constant (~ 2.3 x 10^17 kg/m^3) for all nuclei
II. Nuclides having identical atomic number Z but different mass numbers A
III. Nuclides having identical mass number A but different atomic numbers Z
IV. R = R_0 * A^(1/3) where R_0 approx 1.2 fm
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Nuclear radius R): Nuclear volume is directly proportional to nucleon number A, so R is proportional to A^(1/3).. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Nuclear matter density rho): Density rho = M / V = (A m_N) / [(4/3) pi R_0^3 A] = 3 m_N / (4 pi R_0^3), independent of mass number A.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Isotopes): They contain the same number of protons and exhibit identical chemical properties.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Isobars): They have the same total number of nucleons but belong to different chemical elements.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the radioactive decay relations in List I with their mathematical formulas in List II:
List I:
A. Half-life T_half in terms of decay constant lambda
B. Mean lifetime tau in terms of decay constant lambda
C. Sample activity A(t) at time t
D. Fraction of nuclei remaining undecayed after n half-lives
List II:
I. T_half = ln(2) / lambda approx 0.693 / lambda
II. N / N_0 = (1/2)^n = 2^(-n)
III. tau = 1 / lambda = T_half / ln(2) approx 1.443 * T_half
IV. A(t) = lambda * N(t) = A_0 * e^(-lambda * t)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Half-life T_half in terms of decay constant lambda): Time required for half of the initial radioactive nuclei to decay.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Mean lifetime tau in terms of decay constant lambda): Average lifetime of a radioactive nucleus before decaying.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Sample activity A(t) at time t): Activity is the rate of nuclear disintegrations per second (-dN/dt).. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Fraction of nuclei remaining undecayed after n half-lives): Every half-life halves the remaining population of undecayed radioactive nuclei.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
In Rutherford alpha scattering by a heavy nucleus of atomic number Z, match the scattering parameters in List I with their descriptions or dependencies in List II:
List I:
A. Distance of closest approach r_0 for head-on collision (b=0)
B. Dependence of r_0 on the kinetic energy K of alpha particle
C. Differential scattering cross-section angular dependence dsigma/dOmega
D. Impact parameter b for scattering angle theta = 180 degrees
List II:
I. Proportional to 1 / sin^4(theta / 2)
II. r_0 = (1 / 4*pi*epsilon_0) * (2*Z*e^2 / K)
III. b = 0
IV. Inversely proportional to K (r_0 proportional to K^-1)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Distance of closest approach r_0 for head-on collision (b=0)): All initial kinetic energy K converts into electrostatic potential energy at the turning point.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Dependence of r_0 on the kinetic energy K of alpha particle): Doubling the incident kinetic energy halves the distance of closest approach.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Differential scattering cross-section angular dependence dsigma/dOmega): Rutherford scattering formula predicts count rate falling steeply with scattering angle theta.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Impact parameter b for scattering angle theta = 180 degrees): A head-on collision has zero impact parameter, resulting in exact backward reflection.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the transitions in the hydrogen atom in List I with the emitted photon wavelength or energy in List II (Rydberg constant R approx 1.097 x 10^7 m^-1):
List I:
A. First line of Lyman series (n=2 -> n=1, Lyman-alpha)
B. First line of Balmer series (n=3 -> n=2, H-alpha)
C. Series limit of Lyman series (n=infinity -> n=1)
D. Series limit of Balmer series (n=infinity -> n=2)
List II:
I. lambda = 36 / (5*R) approx 6563 A, Delta E = 1.89 eV
II. lambda = 4 / R approx 3646 A, Delta E = 3.4 eV
III. lambda = 4 / (3*R) approx 1216 A, Delta E = 10.2 eV
IV. lambda = 1 / R approx 912 A, Delta E = 13.6 eV
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (First line of Lyman series (n=2 -> n=1, Lyman-alpha)): 1/lambda = R(1/1^2 - 1/2^2) = 3R/4, Delta E = 13.6(1 - 1/4) = 10.2 eV.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (First line of Balmer series (n=3 -> n=2, H-alpha)): 1/lambda = R(1/4 - 1/9) = 5R/36, Delta E = 13.6(1/4 - 1/9) = 1.89 eV.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Series limit of Lyman series (n=infinity -> n=1)): 1/lambda = R(1 - 0) = R, Delta E = 13.6 eV.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Series limit of Balmer series (n=infinity -> n=2)): 1/lambda = R(1/4 - 0) = R/4, Delta E = 13.6/4 = 3.4 eV.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the energy quantities of an electron in orbit n of a hydrogen atom in List I with their relations and values in List II:
List I:
A. Kinetic energy K_n
B. Potential energy U_n
C. Total energy E_n
D. Change in kinetic and potential energy when transitioning from n=1 to n=2
List II:
I. Delta K = -10.2 eV and Delta U = +20.4 eV
II. E_n = K_n + U_n = -13.6 / n^2 eV
III. U_n = 2*E_n = -27.2 / n^2 eV
IV. K_n = -E_n = +13.6 / n^2 eV
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Kinetic energy K_n): Kinetic energy is always positive and equals the magnitude of total energy.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Potential energy U_n): By the virial theorem for 1/r electrostatic potential, U_n = 2 E_n = -2 K_n.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Total energy E_n): Negative bound state energy indicates stability of the atomic electron.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Change in kinetic and potential energy when transitioning from n=1 to n=2): K_1 = 13.6, K_2 = 3.4 implies Delta K = -10.2 eV; U_1 = -27.2, U_2 = -6.8 implies Delta U = +20.4 eV.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the properties of single-electron hydrogen-like ions in List I with their values in List II (r_0 = 0.529 A is Bohr radius of hydrogen):
List I:
A. Radius of the first Bohr orbit in He+ ion (Z=2)
B. Ionization energy of Li2+ ion (Z=3) from ground state
C. Orbital speed of electron in first orbit of Be3+ ion (Z=4)
D. Ratio of orbital frequency of revolution f(He+, n=1) / f(H, n=1)
List II:
I. E = 13.6 x 3^2 = 122.4 eV
II. r = r_0 / 2 approx 0.265 A
III. Ratio is 4
IV. v = 4*v_0 approx 8.76 x 10^6 m/s
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Radius of the first Bohr orbit in He+ ion (Z=2)): Formula r_1 = r_0 / Z = 0.529 / 2 = 0.265 A.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Ionization energy of Li2+ ion (Z=3) from ground state): Ionization energy is E_ion = 13.6 Z^2 = 13.6 * 9 = 122.4 eV.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Orbital speed of electron in first orbit of Be3+ ion (Z=4)): v_1 = Z v_0 = 4 * (2.19e6) = 8.76e6 m/s.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Ratio of orbital frequency of revolution f(He+, n=1) / f(H, n=1)): Frequency of revolution f proportional to Z^2 / n^3. For Z=2 vs Z=1, ratio is 2^2 / 1^2 = 4.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the nuclear reactions and binding energy concepts in List I with their descriptions in List II:
List I:
A. Mass defect Delta m of a nuclide (A, Z)X
B. Maximum of the binding energy per nucleon curve (A approx 56, Fe-56)
C. Average energy released per fission of a U-235 nucleus
D. Energy released in D-T fusion (2H + 3H -> 4He + n)
List II:
I. approx 17.6 MeV
II. ~ 8.75 MeV/nucleon, indicating maximum nuclear stability
III. Delta m = [Z*m_p + (A-Z)*m_n] - M_nucleus
IV. approx 200 MeV
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Mass defect Delta m of a nuclide (A, Z)X): Difference between the sum of individual free nucleon masses and the actual bound nuclear mass.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum of the binding energy per nucleon curve (A approx 56, Fe-56)): Nuclei near iron-56 have the highest binding energy per nucleon and cannot release energy via either fission or fusion.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Average energy released per fission of a U-235 nucleus): Energy release arises because heavy nuclei (BE/A ~ 7.6 MeV) split into intermediate fragments (BE/A ~ 8.5 MeV).. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Energy released in D-T fusion (2H + 3H -> 4He + n)): Alpha particle receives 14.1 MeV and neutron carries away 3.5 MeV.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the nuclear radioactive decay modes in List I with their governing nuclear transformations in List II:
List I:
A. Alpha (alpha) decay of parent (A, Z)X
B. Beta-minus (beta-) decay
C. Beta-plus (beta+) decay
D. Gamma (gamma) decay
List II:
I. Transforms to (A-4, Z-2)Y + alpha with monoenergetic alpha particles
II. Proton converts via p -> n + e^+ + nu_e inside proton-rich nucleus
III. De-excitation from nuclear excited state emitting high-energy gamma photon without changing A or Z
IV. Neutron converts via n -> p + e^- + anti-nu_e, exhibiting continuous electron energy spectrum
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Alpha (alpha) decay of parent (A, Z)X): Loss of 2 protons and 2 neutrons; two-body decay yields discrete line spectrum.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Beta-minus (beta-) decay): Three-body decay with antineutrino sharing the Q-value continuously.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Beta-plus (beta+) decay): Accompanied by neutrino emission and reduction of atomic number Z by 1.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Gamma (gamma) decay): Nuclear isomer drops to a lower energy state by radiating a gamma ray photon.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
In a radioactive series 1 -> 2 -> 3 (stable) with decay constants lambda_1 and lambda_2, match the decay conditions in List I with their mathematical consequences in List II:
List I:
A. Secular equilibrium (lambda_1 << lambda_2, extremely long-lived parent)
B. Time t_max at which daughter population N_2 reaches peak
C. Number of daughter nuclei when daughter is directly stable (lambda_2 = 0)
D. Transient equilibrium (lambda_1 < lambda_2)
List II:
I. N_2(t) = N_1(0) * (1 - e^(-lambda_1 * t))
II. t_max = ln(lambda_2 / lambda_1) / (lambda_2 - lambda_1)
III. Daughter activity exceeds parent activity by constant factor lambda_2 / (lambda_2 - lambda_1)
IV. Activities become equal (A_1 = A_2), with population ratio N_2 / N_1 = lambda_1 / lambda_2
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Secular equilibrium (lambda_1 << lambda_2, extremely long-lived parent)): Since dN_2/dt = lambda_1 N_1 - lambda_2 N_2 = 0, lambda_1 N_1 = lambda_2 N_2.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Time t_max at which daughter population N_2 reaches peak): Setting dN_2/dt = 0 in the Bateman equation yields t_max.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Number of daughter nuclei when daughter is directly stable (lambda_2 = 0)): Every decayed parent nucleus directly becomes a stable daughter nucleus.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Transient equilibrium (lambda_1 < lambda_2)): At long times, N_2(t) = [lambda_1 / (lambda_2 - lambda_1)] * N_1(t).. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the radioactive sample conditions in List I with the corresponding time elapsed or ratio in List II:
List I:
A. Sample activity drops to 12.5% of its initial activity
B. Fraction of initial nuclei decayed during one mean life tau = 1 / lambda
C. Sample activity drops to 1% of initial activity
D. Ratio of activities of two samples with equal initial nuclei, where T_1 = 2 h and T_2 = 4 h, after t = 4 h
List II:
I. Ratio A_1 / A_2 = 1
II. Time elapsed equals 3 half-lives (t = 3 * T_half)
III. t = ln(100) / lambda approx 6.64 * T_half
IV. 1 - e^(-1) approx 63.2%
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Sample activity drops to 12.5% of its initial activity): 12.5% = 1/8 = (1/2)^3, which corresponds to exactly 3 half-lives.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Fraction of initial nuclei decayed during one mean life tau = 1 / lambda): Undecayed fraction is e^(-lambda tau) = e^(-1) approx 0.368, so decayed fraction is 1 - 0.368 = 0.632.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Sample activity drops to 1% of initial activity): N/N_0 = 10^-2 implies lambda t = ln(100) approx 4.605 implies t = 4.605 / lambda approx 6.64 T_half.. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Ratio of activities of two samples with equal initial nuclei, where T_1 = 2 h and T_2 = 4 h, after t = 4 h): N_1(4) = N_0/4, lambda_1 = ln(2)/2 implies A_1 = N_0 ln(2)/8. N_2(4) = N_0/2, lambda_2 = ln(2)/4 implies A_2 = N_0 ln(2)/8. Ratio is 1.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
When the finite mass M of the nucleus is taken into account, match the system in List I with its reduced mass and physical properties in List II:
List I:
A. Reduced mass formula for an electron of mass m_e orbiting nucleus of mass M
B. Positronium atom (bound state of electron and positron, M = m_e)
C. Muonic hydrogen (muon with mass m_mu approx 207 m_e orbiting a proton)
D. Rydberg constant correction for finite nuclear mass
List II:
I. R_M = R_infinity * [M / (m_e + M)]
II. Bohr orbital radius is reduced by a factor of approx 186
III. mu = m_e * M / (m_e + M) = m_e / (1 + m_e / M)
IV. Reduced mass mu = m_e / 2, ground state binding energy is 6.8 eV
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Reduced mass formula for an electron of mass m_e orbiting nucleus of mass M): Two-body central force problem reduces to single particle of reduced mass mu.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Positronium atom (bound state of electron and positron, M = m_e)): Since mu = m_e / 2, all energy levels are halved compared to hydrogen: E_1 = -13.6 / 2 = -6.8 eV.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Muonic hydrogen (muon with mass m_mu approx 207 m_e orbiting a proton)): Reduced mass mu = (207 * 1836) / (207 + 1836) m_e approx 186 m_e. Radius r proportional to 1/mu shrinks by 186 times.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Rydberg constant correction for finite nuclear mass): Since R proportional to mu, R_M = R_infinity (mu / m_e) = R_infinity * M / (m_e + M).. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the nuclear recoil quantities in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Kinetic energy of alpha particle in alpha decay of stationary nucleus of mass number A
B. Recoil kinetic energy of daughter nucleus in alpha decay
C. Recoil kinetic energy of a nucleus of mass M emitting a gamma photon of energy E_0
D. Actual energy E_gamma of the emitted gamma photon
List II:
I. K_recoil = E_0^2 / (2 * M * c^2)
II. E_gamma = E_0 - E_0^2 / (2 * M * c^2)
III. K_D = (4 / A) * Q
IV. K_alpha = [(A - 4) / A] * Q
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Kinetic energy of alpha particle in alpha decay of stationary nucleus of mass number A): From momentum conservation p_D = p_alpha, K_alpha = [m_D / (m_D + m_alpha)] * Q = [(A-4)/A] * Q.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Recoil kinetic energy of daughter nucleus in alpha decay): Daughter receives remaining energy: K_D = [m_alpha / (m_D + m_alpha)] * Q = (4/A) * Q.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Recoil kinetic energy of a nucleus of mass M emitting a gamma photon of energy E_0): Photon momentum p = E_0 / c. Nucleus recoil kinetic energy is p^2 / (2M) = E_0^2 / (2 M c^2).. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Actual energy E_gamma of the emitted gamma photon): Conservation of energy requires E_0 = E_gamma + K_recoil approx E_gamma + E_0^2 / (2 M c^2).. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the characteristics of continuous and characteristic X-ray spectra in List I with their formulas in List II:
List I:
A. Duane-Hunt cutoff wavelength lambda_min for tube voltage V
B. Moseley's law for K-alpha characteristic X-ray frequency
C. Wavelength of K-alpha X-ray line as a function of atomic number Z
D. Moseley's law for L-alpha line (n=3 -> n=2)
List II:
I. sqrt(nu) = a * (Z - 1)
II. lambda_min = hc / (eV) = 12400 / V(volts) A
III. 1 / lambda_Kalpha = (3/4) * R * (Z - 1)^2
IV. sqrt(nu) = a' * (Z - 7.4)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Duane-Hunt cutoff wavelength lambda_min for tube voltage V): An electron converted entirely into a single bremsstrahlung photon yields lambda_min.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Moseley's law for K-alpha characteristic X-ray frequency): For K-alpha transition (n=2 -> n=1), screening constant is b=1 due to the single remaining 1s electron.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Wavelength of K-alpha X-ray line as a function of atomic number Z): 1/lambda = R (Z-1)^2 (1/1^2 - 1/2^2) = (3/4) R (Z-1)^2.. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Moseley's law for L-alpha line (n=3 -> n=2)): For L-shell transitions, shielding by inner K and L electrons yields screening constant b approx 7.4.. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
In the thermal neutron fission of U-235 releasing approx 200 MeV, match the energy component in List I with its contribution in List II:
List I:
A. Kinetic energy carried by the two main fission fragments
B. Kinetic energy carried by prompt fission neutrons
C. Energy carried by prompt and delayed gamma rays
D. Energy carried away by antineutrinos from subsequent beta- decays
List II:
I. ~ 168 MeV (approx 84% of total energy)
II. ~ 5 MeV (average ~ 2 MeV per neutron)
III. ~ 12 MeV (unrecoverable as heat in reactor)
IV. ~ 15 MeV
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Kinetic energy carried by the two main fission fragments): The large Coulomb repulsion between the newly created fragment nuclei converts into massive fragment kinetic energy.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Kinetic energy carried by prompt fission neutrons): An average of 2.5 prompt neutrons are emitted per fission carrying approx 2 MeV each.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Energy carried by prompt and delayed gamma rays): De-excitation of highly excited fission fragments emits both prompt and delayed gamma photons.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Energy carried away by antineutrinos from subsequent beta- decays): Antineutrinos escape the reactor completely without interacting or contributing to thermal power.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the nuclear fusion concepts in List I with their quantitative relations in List II:
List I:
A. Proton-proton cycle net reaction in stars (4p -> 4He + 2e+ + 2nu_e + 2gamma)
B. Height of Coulomb barrier between two colliding deuterons (R approx 2 fm)
C. Kinetic temperature required for fusion by quantum mechanical tunneling
D. Lawson criterion for D-T thermonuclear fusion power break-even
List II:
I. V_C = e^2 / [4*pi*epsilon_0 * (2R)] approx 360 keV
II. n * tau_E >= 1.5 x 10^20 s*m^-3 at T approx 10-20 keV
III. Q = +26.7 MeV total energy released
IV. T ~ 1.5 x 10^7 K (core of the Sun)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Proton-proton cycle net reaction in stars (4p -> 4He + 2e+ + 2nu_e + 2gamma)): Mass difference between 4 protons and an alpha particle plus positrons corresponds to 26.7 MeV.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Height of Coulomb barrier between two colliding deuterons (R approx 2 fm)): Electrostatic repulsion energy when two deuterons just touch at distance 2R.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Kinetic temperature required for fusion by quantum mechanical tunneling): Wave nature of nucleons allows barrier penetration at energies ~ 10 keV, well below classical barrier.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Lawson criterion for D-T thermonuclear fusion power break-even): Condition on plasma density n and confinement time tau_E for self-sustaining fusion.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the spectral line broadening mechanisms in atomic physics in List I with their descriptions in List II:
List I:
A. Natural linewidth from Heisenberg uncertainty principle (Delta E Delta t >= hbar/2)
B. Doppler broadening due to thermal motion of emitting gas atoms
C. Pressure (collisional) broadening
D. Recoil broadening in Mossbauer effect (unrecoiled emission)
List II:
I. Linewidth increases linearly with gas density and collision frequency
II. Delta nu_nat approx 1 / (2*pi*tau), giving Delta lambda ~ 10^-4 A
III. Recoil momentum absorbed by entire crystal lattice, preserving natural linewidth
IV. Delta nu_D / nu_0 approx sqrt(8 * k_B * T * ln(2) / (M * c^2)) proportional to sqrt(T)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Natural linewidth from Heisenberg uncertainty principle (Delta E Delta t >= hbar/2)): Finite radiative lifetime tau ~ 10^-8 s of excited states creates an intrinsic lower bound on spectral linewidth.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Doppler broadening due to thermal motion of emitting gas atoms): Thermal Maxwellian velocity distribution shifts perceived frequencies via Doppler effect, scaling with sqrt(T).. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Pressure (collisional) broadening): Frequent collisions during radiative emission shorten effective coherent wave-train lifetime.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Recoil broadening in Mossbauer effect (unrecoiled emission)): Embedding nuclei in rigid crystal lattice eliminates recoil energy loss, allowing resonant gamma absorption.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the magnetic dipole and Zeeman effect quantities in List I with their values and expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Bohr magneton (mu_B) for electron orbital motion
B. Nuclear magneton (mu_N)
C. Normal Zeeman splitting of spectral line of frequency nu_0 in magnetic field B
D. Larmor precession frequency of magnetic dipole in magnetic field B
List II:
I. omega_L = e * B / (2 * m_e)
II. mu_N = e*hbar / (2*m_p) approx 5.05 x 10^-27 J/T
III. Delta nu = e * B / (4 * pi * m_e)
IV. mu_B = e*hbar / (2*m_e) approx 9.274 x 10^-24 J/T
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Bohr magneton (mu_B) for electron orbital motion): Fundamental quantum of electronic magnetic dipole moment.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Nuclear magneton (mu_N)): Nuclear magnetic moments are ~ 2000 times smaller than electronic moments due to large proton mass.. Therefore, B corresponds to II.
Step 3: Match item C (Normal Zeeman splitting of spectral line of frequency nu_0 in magnetic field B): Spectral line splits into three components: nu_0 and nu_0 +/- Delta nu.. Therefore, C corresponds to III.
Step 4: Match item D (Larmor precession frequency of magnetic dipole in magnetic field B): Torque tau = mu x B causes precession of angular momentum vector at Larmor frequency.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
A radioisotope X decays simultaneously via two branching pathways: alpha decay with decay constant lambda_alpha and beta decay with decay constant lambda_beta. Match the composite decay quantities in List I with their expressions in List II:
List I:
A. Total effective decay constant lambda_total
B. Total effective half-life T_total in terms of individual half-lives T_alpha and T_beta
C. Branching ratio (fraction) of decays that proceed via alpha emission
D. Ratio of number of emitted alpha particles to beta particles at any elapsed time
List II:
I. lambda_total = lambda_alpha + lambda_beta
II. Fraction_alpha = lambda_alpha / (lambda_alpha + lambda_beta)
III. T_total = T_alpha * T_beta / (T_alpha + T_beta)
IV. N_alpha(t) / N_beta(t) = lambda_alpha / lambda_beta
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Total effective decay constant lambda_total): Total rate of disintegration is -dN/dt = (lambda_alpha + lambda_beta) N.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Total effective half-life T_total in terms of individual half-lives T_alpha and T_beta): Since lambda_total = lambda_alpha + lambda_beta, ln(2)/T_total = ln(2)/T_alpha + ln(2)/T_beta.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Branching ratio (fraction) of decays that proceed via alpha emission): Fraction of parent nuclei decaying by alpha mode is proportional to lambda_alpha.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Ratio of number of emitted alpha particles to beta particles at any elapsed time): At every instant, rate of alpha emission to beta emission is strictly lambda_alpha / lambda_beta.. Therefore, D corresponds to IV.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the materials in List I with their forbidden energy band gap (E_g) characteristics at room temperature (300 K) in List II:
List I:
A. Good conductor (e.g. Copper, Aluminum)
B. Insulator (e.g. Diamond)
C. Silicon crystal semiconductor
D. Germanium crystal semiconductor
List II:
I. Moderate band gap (E_g approx 0.67 eV)
II. Valence and conduction bands overlap (E_g approx 0 eV)
III. Very wide band gap (E_g approx 5.4 eV)
IV. Moderate band gap (E_g approx 1.1 eV)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Good conductor (e.g. Copper, Aluminum)): Conduction electrons can move freely under any electric field with no thermal activation required.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Insulator (e.g. Diamond)): Thermal energy at room temperature (k_B T approx 0.026 eV) is far too small to bridge E_g > 3 eV.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Silicon crystal semiconductor): Moderate thermal excitation creates a usable number of electron-hole pairs.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Germanium crystal semiconductor): Smaller band gap than silicon; higher intrinsic conductivity at room temperature.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the semiconductor types in List I with their majority charge carriers and properties in List II:
List I:
A. Intrinsic semiconductor
B. n-type extrinsic semiconductor
C. p-type extrinsic semiconductor
D. Mass action law under thermal equilibrium
List II:
I. Majority carriers are holes (n_h >> n_e), doped with trivalent acceptors
II. n_e * n_h = n_i^2, valid for both intrinsic and doped semiconductors
III. Carrier densities are equal: n_e = n_h = n_i
IV. Majority carriers are electrons (n_e >> n_h), doped with pentavalent donors
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Intrinsic semiconductor): Thermally generated electrons in conduction band equal holes in valence band.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (n-type extrinsic semiconductor): Impurity atoms like P, As, Sb donate extra conduction electrons.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (p-type extrinsic semiconductor): Impurity atoms like B, Al, In create vacant covalent bond positions (holes).. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Mass action law under thermal equilibrium): Product of electron and hole concentrations is independent of doping level at a given temperature.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the basic two-input logic gates in List I with their Boolean operations in List II:
List I:
A. AND gate
B. OR gate
C. NOT gate
D. NAND gate
List II:
I. Y = A + B (Output is 1 if either or both inputs are 1)
II. Y = bar(A) (Output is the logical inversion of the single input)
III. Y = bar(A * B) (Universal gate; output is 0 only when both inputs are 1)
IV. Y = A * B (Output is 1 only when both inputs are 1)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (AND gate): Logical conjunction; output is HIGH if and only if all inputs are HIGH.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (OR gate): Logical disjunction; output is LOW only when all inputs are LOW.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (NOT gate): Inverter; changes 0 to 1 and 1 to 0.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (NAND gate): Complement of AND gate; can be used to construct all other logic functions.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the p-n junction operating conditions in List I with their depletion layer behavior in List II:
List I:
A. Unbiased p-n junction in equilibrium
B. Forward biased p-n junction (V > 0 applied to p-side)
C. Reverse biased p-n junction (V > 0 applied to n-side)
D. Depletion layer composition
List II:
I. Built-in potential barrier V_bi forms, with diffusion current balancing drift current
II. Composed solely of unneutralized immobile ionized donor and acceptor ions, devoid of free carriers
III. Barrier height reduces to V_bi - V, depletion width narrows, and large diffusion current flows
IV. Barrier height increases to V_bi + V, depletion width widens, and tiny minority drift current flows
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Unbiased p-n junction in equilibrium): Majority carrier diffusion establishes fixed donor/acceptor ion space charge.. Therefore, A corresponds to I.
Step 2: Match item B (Forward biased p-n junction (V > 0 applied to p-side)): Applied field opposes built-in field, allowing majority carriers to cross junction easily.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Reverse biased p-n junction (V > 0 applied to n-side)): Applied field reinforces built-in field, shutting off majority carrier diffusion.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Depletion layer composition): Free electrons and holes are swept away by the intense built-in electric field.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option D.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the temperature dependence of electrical properties in List I with their physical descriptions in List II:
List I:
A. Intrinsic carrier concentration n_i(T)
B. Temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) for semiconductors
C. Temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) for pure metals
D. Extrinsic semiconductor in exhaustion (saturation) region
List II:
I. Positive (alpha > 0), resistance increases with increasing temperature
II. Increases exponentially as T^(3/2) * exp(-E_g / (2 * k_B * T))
III. Carrier density remains roughly constant equal to dopant density N_D or N_A
IV. Negative (alpha < 0), resistance decreases with increasing temperature
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Intrinsic carrier concentration n_i(T)): Rising temperature drastically boosts covalent bond rupture and electron-hole pair generation.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) for semiconductors): Exponential surge in carrier density dominates over any reduction in carrier mobility.. Therefore, B corresponds to IV.
Step 3: Match item C (Temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) for pure metals): Free carrier concentration is constant; increased lattice vibrations shorten mean relaxation time.. Therefore, C corresponds to I.
Step 4: Match item D (Extrinsic semiconductor in exhaustion (saturation) region): All dopant impurity atoms are already ionized, while intrinsic excitation is still negligible.. Therefore, D corresponds to III.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to Option B.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the transport quantities in semiconductor physics in List I with their formulas and relations in List II:
List I:
A. Total electrical conductivity sigma of a semiconductor
B. Mobility comparison between electrons mu_e and holes mu_h
C. Einstein relation connecting diffusion constant D and mobility mu
D. Drift current density J in electric field E
List II:
I. mu_e > mu_h because electrons in conduction band have lower effective mass than holes
II. vec(J) = sigma * vec(E) = e * (n_e * mu_e + n_h * mu_h) * vec(E)
III. sigma = e * (n_e * mu_e + n_h * mu_h)
IV. D_e / mu_e = D_h / mu_h = k_B * T / e
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Total electrical conductivity sigma of a semiconductor): Both conduction electrons and valence holes contribute additively to total current.. Therefore, A corresponds to III.
Step 2: Match item B (Mobility comparison between electrons mu_e and holes mu_h): Conduction band curvature is sharper than valence band, giving electrons higher mobility.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
Step 3: Match item C (Einstein relation connecting diffusion constant D and mobility mu): Fundamental thermodynamic relationship between thermal diffusion and field drift.. Therefore, C corresponds to IV.
Step 4: Match item D (Drift current density J in electric field E): Ohm's law in point form for semiconductor transport.. Therefore, D corresponds to II.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II, which corresponds to Option C.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the rectifier circuits and parameters in List I with their quantitative characteristics in List II (for input AC frequency f):
List I:
A. Maximum theoretical efficiency of half-wave rectifier
B. Maximum theoretical efficiency of full-wave rectifier
C. Output ripple frequency of full-wave rectifier
D. Ripple factor gamma of half-wave rectifier
List II:
I. 1.21
II. 2f
III. 81.2%
IV. 40.6%
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Maximum theoretical efficiency of half-wave rectifier): eta_max = 0.406 / (1 + r_f/R_L) <= 40.6%.. Therefore, A corresponds to IV.
Step 2: Match item B (Maximum theoretical efficiency of full-wave rectifier): eta_max = 0.812 / (1 + r_f/R_L) <= 81.2%, double that of a half-wave rectifier.. Therefore, B corresponds to III.
Step 3: Match item C (Output ripple frequency of full-wave rectifier): Output pulses twice every full AC cycle, so ripple frequency is 2f.. Therefore, C corresponds to II.
Step 4: Match item D (Ripple factor gamma of half-wave rectifier): Ripple factor gamma = sqrt((I_rms / I_dc)^2 - 1) = sqrt((pi/2)^2 - 1) approx 1.21.. Therefore, D corresponds to I.
Conclusion: The correct matching is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I, which corresponds to Option A.

subject: Physics
questionText:
Match the Zener diode features and breakdown mechanisms in List I with their descriptions in List II:
List I:
A. Zener breakdown mechanism (V_Z < 6 V)
B. Avalanche breakdown mechanism (V_Z > 6 V)
C. Temperature coefficient of breakdown voltage
D. Zener diode as a voltage regulator
List II:
I. Impact ionization by accelerated minority carriers dislodging secondary electron-hole pairs
II. Direct quantum mechanical tunneling of valence electrons across narrow depletion region
III. Operates in reverse breakdown where voltage remains constant over wide variations in current
IV. Negative for Zener breakdown, positive for Avalanche breakdown
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation:
Step 1: Match item A (Zener breakdown mechanism (V_Z < 6 V)): Occurs in heavily doped junctions where electric field exceeds 10^6 V/m.. Therefore, A corresponds to II.
Step 2: Match item B (Avalanche breakdown mechanism (V_Z > 6 V)): Occurs in lightly doped junctions with wider depletion regions.. Therefore, B corresponds to I.
